Moscow holds a military parade on Red Square, families march with portraits of relatives who fought, and the evening ends with fireworks.

slogans.en: Victory forged in courage and sacrifice.

descriptions.en: World Migratory Bird Day celebrates the birds that travel thousands of kilometres between breeding and wintering grounds each year. It is held twice a year, in May and October, to follow the spring and autumn migrations along different flyways. Organised under UN wildlife treaties with partners around the world, it carries a new theme each year and highlights threats such as habitat loss, pollution and light at night. People mark it with birdwatching walks, festivals, talks and school activities.

World Lupus Day on 10 May raises awareness of lupus, a chronic autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues, such as the skin, joints and kidneys. Lupus is hard to diagnose because its symptoms, like fatigue, joint pain and a rash across the cheeks, come and go and resemble other illnesses. Most people with lupus are women, often diagnosed in their younger adult years. Patient groups use the day to call for earlier diagnosis, better care and more research, and supporters wear purple.

International Nurses Day falls on 12 May, the birthday of Florence Nightingale, who was born in 1820 and is seen as the founder of modern nursing. During the Crimean War she ran the hospital at the Selimiye Barracks in Üsküdar, Istanbul, where she improved hygiene and care for wounded soldiers. The International Council of Nurses promotes the day each year with a theme. Hospitals, schools and health ministries thank nurses for their work, and in Türkiye the day opens Nursing Week.

slogans.en: Nurses: A Voice to Lead — Health for All

descriptions.en: May 14 is Scientific Pharmacy Day in Turkey, celebrating the pharmacist's role as a healthcare professional grounded in science. The date commemorates the founding of the first modern school of pharmacy in Turkey. Pharmacists across the country are recognised for their contributions to public health, medication safety, and evidence-based practice.

May 14 is Farmers' Day in Turkey, honouring the farmers and farm workers who feed the nation. The date is the anniversary of the general election of May 14, 1950, in which the votes of rural, farming communities played a decisive part. The day recognises agriculture's vital place in Turkey's economy, culture and food security, and the hard work behind every harvest. It is marked with ceremonies, messages from officials and farmers' organisations, and events in villages and towns across the country.

Israel Independence Day, Yom Ha'atzmaut, marks the declaration of the State of Israel by David Ben-Gurion in Tel Aviv on 14 May 1948. It is observed on the 5th of Iyar in the Hebrew calendar, so its date on the Gregorian calendar changes from year to year. The day begins at sunset straight after Memorial Day for fallen soldiers, with a torch-lighting ceremony on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem. Israelis celebrate with fireworks, air force flyovers, family picnics and barbecues, and the Israel Prize is awarded.

slogans.en: Am Yisrael Chai! (The People of Israel Live!)

descriptions.en: The International Day of Families on 15 May celebrates families as the first place where people find care, support and a sense of belonging. The UN General Assembly proclaimed the day in 1993, and it has been observed every year since 1994. Each year it focuses on a theme, such as balancing work and family life, child and elder care, or how social and economic change affects households. Governments, schools and community groups hold talks and family events, and many people simply spend the day together.

slogans.en: Families and climate action: focus on SDGs.

descriptions.en: Nakba Day, held on 15 May, remembers the mass displacement of Palestinians during the war of 1947–1949, when more than 700,000 people fled or were driven from their homes and hundreds of villages were emptied. The date falls the day after the State of Israel was proclaimed in May 1948, and "Nakba" means "catastrophe" in Arabic. Palestinians and their supporters around the world mark it with marches, sirens and moments of silence, and many carry old house keys as a symbol of the homes they hope to return to.

The International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia, known as IDAHOBIT, is held on 17 May. The date recalls 17 May 1990, when the World Health Organization removed homosexuality from its classification of diseases. First marked in 2005, the day draws attention to the discrimination and violence that LGBTI+ people still face in many countries. It is observed with rallies, rainbow flags on public buildings, panel discussions and campaigns for equal rights and safety.

slogans.en: Our bodies, our lives, our rights.

descriptions.en: Norway's Constitution Day, known as Syttende mai, falls on 17 May and is the country's national day. It marks the signing of the Norwegian Constitution at Eidsvoll on 17 May 1814, one of the oldest written constitutions still in use. Rather than military parades, the day belongs to children: schoolchildren march through every town waving flags, while the royal family greets the procession from the palace balcony in Oslo. People wear bunad, the traditional costume, and the day ends with ice cream, hot dogs and games.

Endangered Species Day draws attention to the plants and animals at risk of disappearing and to the people working to save them. It began in the United States in 2006 and is now marked by zoos, aquariums, parks and schools in many countries. Habitat loss, poaching, pollution and climate change push more species toward extinction every year, and the day shows that recovery is possible when they are protected. People join guided walks, clean-ups, tree plantings and talks about local wildlife.

International Museum Day, held on or around 18 May, celebrates museums as places of cultural exchange, learning and mutual understanding. The International Council of Museums (ICOM) created the day in 1977 and chooses a new theme for it every year. Museums around the world take part with free or reduced entry, guided tours, workshops and evening openings. It is a good day to visit a museum you have never been to, or to see a familiar one with fresh eyes.

names.en: Atatürk Commemoration, Youth and Sports Day (Turkey)

descriptions.en: May 19 commemorates Mustafa Kemal Atatürk's arrival in Samsun in 1919, which marked the beginning of the Turkish War of Independence. The day is also dedicated to the youth of Turkey and to sports, reflecting Atatürk's famous quote entrusting the nation's future to its young people. It is celebrated with youth festivals, athletic events, and ceremonies across the country.

slogans.en: Muhtaç olduğun kudret, damarlarındaki asil kanda mevcuttur.

descriptions.en: Malcolm X Day falls on 19 May, the birthday of Malcolm X, who was born in Omaha, Nebraska, in 1925. He became one of the most powerful voices for Black dignity, self-reliance and human rights in the United States before he was assassinated in New York in 1965. The day is not a federal holiday, but some cities, schools and communities mark it. People gather for lectures, readings from his autobiography and community events that reflect on his ideas and legacy.

slogans.en: By any means necessary — stand for justice.

descriptions.en: World Bee Day, on 20 May, highlights how much our food and ecosystems depend on bees and other pollinators. The United Nations proclaimed the day in 2017 at Slovenia's initiative, and it was first observed in 2018. The date is the birthday of Anton Janša, an 18th-century Slovenian pioneer of modern beekeeping. People mark it by planting flowers bees love, buying honey from local beekeepers, avoiding pesticides in their gardens and learning about the threats pollinators face.

World Tea Day on 21 May celebrates one of the most widely drunk beverages on Earth and the millions of people who grow and pick it. The UN General Assembly proclaimed the day in 2019, and the Food and Agriculture Organization leads its observance, focusing on fair livelihoods for small growers and sustainable farming. People mark it by brewing a favourite tea, trying a new one and sharing a pot with friends.

World Fish Migration Day raises awareness of migratory fish and the free-flowing rivers they need to survive. Species such as salmon, eels and sturgeon travel long distances between feeding and spawning grounds, but dams, weirs and other barriers block their way, and many populations have fallen sharply. The day is coordinated by an international network of conservation groups, researchers and local organisers. Events take place along rivers around the world, from guided walks and fish counts to the removal of old barriers.

slogans.en: Open rivers, migratory fish — a healthy planet.

descriptions.en: The International Day for Biological Diversity on 22 May draws attention to the variety of life on Earth, from soil microbes to forests and coral reefs, and to how fast it is being lost. The date marks the adoption of the text of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity on 22 May 1992. Schools, parks and conservation groups mark it with nature walks, tree planting, species counts and talks on protecting habitats.

Bitcoin Pizza Day recalls 22 May 2010, when programmer Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 bitcoins for two pizzas, the first well-known purchase of a physical good with the cryptocurrency. At the time the coins were worth only a few dozen dollars; their later value turned the deal into a famous story. Crypto fans mark the day by ordering pizza, sometimes paying in bitcoin, and joking about the most expensive pizzas ever bought.

slogans.en: The most expensive pizzas in history.

descriptions.en: Harvey Milk Day honors the birthday and legacy of Harvey Milk, the first openly gay person elected to public office in California. Made a state holiday in 2009, it celebrates his pioneering role in LGBTQ+ rights through education, flag-raisings, and advocacy. Elected to San Francisco's Board of Supervisors in 1977, Milk was assassinated in 1978 but remains an enduring symbol of hope.

Yemen Unification Day is the country's national day, marking 22 May 1990, when the Yemen Arab Republic in the north and the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen in the south merged into the Republic of Yemen. Unity was proclaimed in Aden, ending decades of division between the two states. The day is a public holiday, marked with flag-raising, official speeches, parades and celebrations of a shared Yemeni identity.

On May 23, 1949, the Basic Law (Grundgesetz) — the constitution of the Federal Republic of Germany — was promulgated, laying the foundation for a democratic, federal state. Shaped by the lessons of the Nazi era, the Grundgesetz enshrines fundamental rights as inviolable and directly binding on all state authority. It is considered one of the most successful constitutions in history.

World Turtle Day on 23 May celebrates turtles and tortoises, reptiles that have outlived the dinosaurs yet now face habitat loss, pollution, poaching and the pet trade. The day was started by the US group American Tortoise Rescue in 2000 to encourage people to learn about and protect them. People mark it by helping turtles cross roads safely, cleaning beaches, supporting rescue centres and, often, dressing up in green.

Towel Day on 25 May is a tribute to Douglas Adams, author of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Fans first held it in 2001, two weeks after his death, as a playful farewell. In the book a towel is the most useful thing an interstellar hitchhiker can carry. So on this day readers around the world carry a towel to work, school or the shops, and swap their favourite quotes, like "Don't Panic".

slogans.en: Don't panic. And carry a towel.

descriptions.en: World Football Day on 25 May celebrates the world's most popular sport and its power to bring people together. The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed it in 2024. The date marks the centenary of the 1924 Paris Olympic football tournament, the first international tournament with teams from every region of the world. People mark it with friendly matches, school and community games, and events promoting fair play, inclusion and peace.

slogans.en: The Beautiful Game Belongs to Everyone.

descriptions.en: World Otter Day raises awareness about the threats facing otters worldwide. All 13 otter species face varying levels of threat from habitat loss, pollution, hunting, and illegal trade. Otters are vital ecosystem engineers.

Geek Pride Day on 25 May celebrates everyone with a deep, joyful passion for science, technology, games, comics or science fiction. It began in Spain in 2006 as Día del Orgullo Friki and soon spread online around the world. The date honours the 1977 premiere of Star Wars and falls on Towel Day too. Fans mark it with costumes, board-game and film nights, and by proudly sharing the things they love.

slogans.en: Be proud to be a geek!

descriptions.en: National Wine Day on May 25 celebrates wine in all its forms, from red and white to rosé and sparkling. Wine is one of humanity's oldest crafted drinks: the earliest known traces of winemaking from grapes, found in Georgia in the South Caucasus, date back about 8,000 years. Over the centuries it has become part of meals, religious rites and celebrations in many cultures. People mark the day by sharing a bottle with friends, trying a new grape variety or visiting a nearby winery, always in moderation.

slogans.en: Raise a glass to the world’s oldest pleasure.

descriptions.en: May Revolution Day on 25 May is an Argentine national holiday recalling the week of May 1810 in Buenos Aires, when residents removed the Spanish viceroy and set up the First Junta, the first local government. It began the road to independence, formally declared on 9 July 1816. Argentines mark it with flag displays, a Te Deum at Buenos Aires Cathedral, school events and bowls of locro, empanadas and hot chocolate.

slogans.en: The week that began a nation.

descriptions.en: Jordan Independence Day on 25 May celebrates the birth of the Hashemite Kingdom as a sovereign state. On that day in 1946 the British mandate over Transjordan came to an end and Emir Abdullah was proclaimed king. It is a national public holiday across the country. Streets and buildings are draped in the red, white, green and black flag, and the day brings military parades, concerts and fireworks over Amman.

World Redhead Day on May 26th celebrates one of nature's rarest hair colors — found in only 1–2% of the world's population. What began with Dutch artist Bart Rouwenhorst's 2005 casting call for red-haired models, which unexpectedly drew huge crowds, grew into annual Redhead Days festivals in the Netherlands and eventually a global movement. The day champions red hair in all its shades — from strawberry blonde to deep auburn — and turns what was once a target for teasing into a source of community pride.

slogans.en: Be rare, be radiant — embrace your red.

descriptions.en: World Hamburger Day on 28 May is an informal food holiday for one of the world's best-loved dishes. Nobody knows exactly who invented the hamburger, and several American towns still claim it, but the beef patty in a bun took off in the United States around the turn of the 20th century. Today it comes in endless versions, from classic cheeseburgers to chicken and veggie burgers. People celebrate with backyard grills, burger-joint visits and homemade creations.

slogans.en: Grill It. Stack It. Devour It.

descriptions.en: Brunettes Day on May 28 is a lighthearted celebration of people with brown hair, from light chestnut to deep espresso. Its origins are unclear, but it has caught on online as a companion to the other hair colour days. Brown and black hair are by far the most common colours in the world, so this is a day for the many to enjoy what they often take for granted. People mark it by sharing photos, celebrating famous brunettes or simply giving their own shade some credit.

slogans.en: Dark hair, bright spirit — today is yours.

descriptions.en: World No Tobacco Day, held every year on May 31, highlights the harm tobacco does to health and the steps that can cut its use. It was created by the member states of the World Health Organization in 1987, and each year brings a new theme. Health services run campaigns and quit-smoking support, governments are urged to adopt stronger tobacco controls, and many smokers pick the day to put down their last cigarette.

National Smile Day, on May 31, celebrates the simplest gesture people share across every language and culture. A smile can ease tension, make a stranger feel welcome and turn an ordinary moment into a warm one, and smiles tend to be contagious, spreading from one face to the next. Research also links smiling and laughter with lower stress and a better mood. Mark the day by smiling at the people you pass, sending a funny message to a friend or doing something that makes someone else smile.

World Parrot Day on May 31 was established in 2004 by the World Parrot Trust to celebrate these remarkable birds and raise awareness about their conservation. Many parrot species are threatened by deforestation, illegal trade, and habitat destruction. Today, learn about their intelligence, beauty, and vital role in forest ecosystems.

slogans.en: Protect the world's most colorful voices.

descriptions.en: World Foster Day on May 31 draws attention to foster care and to the children who cannot safely live with their own families. It celebrates the foster carers who open their homes, along with the social workers, teachers and mentors who stand beside these children, and it gives a platform to people who grew up in care. The day argues that every child deserves a safe, loving family setting rather than an institution, and many organisations use it to encourage more people to become foster carers.

slogans.en: Every child deserves a safe place to call home.

descriptions.en: Blonde Hair Day on May 31 is a lighthearted celebration of fair hair, from pale platinum to warm honey. Natural blonde hair is rare worldwide and most common in northern Europe; in 2014 scientists traced one common cause to a small genetic change near the KITLG gene. Blonde hair has long shaped art and film, from Renaissance paintings to Jean Harlow, Hollywood's first "platinum blonde". People mark the day by sharing photos, trying a new shade or simply enjoying their own colour, natural or not.

slogans.en: Golden roots, timeless style — celebrate your light.

descriptions.en: African American Music Appreciation Month, celebrated every June, honors the profound contributions of Black musicians across jazz, gospel, rhythm and blues, and hip-hop. Founded in 1979 by President Jimmy Carter at the urging of songwriter Kenny Gamble, it was renamed by President Barack Obama in 2009 to reflect its broader significance. From Louis Armstrong to Beyoncé, Black artists have shaped the sound of American culture and driven global music movements.

slogans.en: The music that moved the world.

descriptions.en: International Children's Day is celebrated on June 1 in many countries. It was first proclaimed at the World Conference for the Well-being of Children in Geneva in 1925. The day recognizes children's rights and promotes their welfare.

slogans.en: Every child has the right to a happy childhood.

descriptions.en: World Milk Day on June 1 celebrates milk as one of the world's most widely consumed foods and the dairy sector that produces it. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations established the day in 2001. Farmers, dairies, schools and nutrition groups mark it with farm visits, tastings and events about milk's role in a healthy diet, and about the millions of livelihoods that depend on dairy farming.

The Global Day of Parents on June 1 honours mothers, fathers and everyone who raises children, for the care and sacrifice they give throughout their lives. The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed the day in 2012, recognising the family as the main place where children grow up and are protected. People mark it by thanking their parents, spending time together as a family and drawing attention to the support parents need.

Pride Month is celebrated every June to honour LGBTQ+ people and their long struggle for equal rights. It recalls the Stonewall uprising, which began on June 28, 1969, when patrons of a New York bar resisted a police raid and sparked a new wave of activism. Today the month is marked with Pride marches, festivals, talks and gatherings in cities around the world, celebrating love, identity and the right to live openly.

slogans.en: Love is love — every color of the rainbow.

descriptions.en: National Adopt a Cat Month, observed every June in the United States, encourages people to give a home to a cat waiting in a shelter. June falls in the middle of kitten season, when shelters fill up with litters born in spring and need adopters most. Shelters and rescue groups hold adoption events and sometimes lower their fees, while future owners are reminded that adopting a cat is a commitment for many years.

slogans.en: Give a cat a forever home.

descriptions.en: National Olive Day, on June 1 in the United States, celebrates one of the oldest cultivated fruits. People in the eastern Mediterranean were growing olive trees thousands of years ago, and the olive is botanically a stone fruit, too bitter to eat straight from the tree until it is cured in brine, salt or water. Today there are hundreds of varieties, and Turkey is one of the world's largest producers. Celebrate with a bowl of olives at breakfast, a drizzle of good olive oil or a classic Mediterranean dish.

Wear a Dress Day is a light-hearted invitation to put on a dress and enjoy the simple pleasure of getting dressed up. It falls at the start of summer in the northern hemisphere, when light fabrics and bright prints come out of the wardrobe. The day is open to everyone, whatever their gender or style, and celebrates clothes as a form of self-expression. People mark it by wearing a favourite dress to work or school, trying something new, or sharing their outfits with friends online.

slogans.en: Wear it, feel it, own it.

descriptions.en: Say Something Nice Day, on June 1, asks everyone to offer at least one sincere compliment or kind word to the people around them. It began in North Charleston, South Carolina, where Mayor Keith Summey proclaimed it in 2006 at the urging of the author Dr. Mitch Carnell, who had long spoken out against everyday negativity at work and at home. People mark it by thanking a colleague, praising someone's good work or leaving a kind note, small gestures that cost nothing and can lift someone's whole day.

slogans.en: Kind words cost nothing and mean everything.

descriptions.en: Dinosaur Day on June 1 celebrates the prehistoric giants that ruled Earth for over 180 million years. Humanity's fascination with dinosaurs dates to 1677, when Oxford professor Robert Plot discovered the first fossil bone — though he mistook it for a giant human's. It wasn't until 1842 that Sir Richard Owen coined the term 'Dinosauria' (meaning 'terrible lizard'). Today, birds are recognized as living theropod dinosaurs, meaning dinosaurs never truly went extinct.

slogans.en: Millions of years gone, never forgotten.

descriptions.en: Italian Republic Day, Festa della Repubblica, on June 2 marks the referendum of 1946, when Italians voted to end the monarchy and make the country a republic. It was the first national vote in which Italian women could take part. In Rome the President lays a wreath at the Altare della Patria, a military parade passes along Via dei Fori Imperiali, and the Frecce Tricolori jets paint the sky green, white and red.

Leave the Office Earlier Day, held on June 2, encourages people to finish their work efficiently and head home a little sooner than usual. It is credited to productivity speaker Laura Stack, who wanted to show that working smarter, not longer, brings better results. People mark it by planning their day carefully, cutting needless meetings and using the extra time for family, friends, rest or a walk in the early summer light.

World Bicycle Day on June 3 celebrates the bicycle, a simple, affordable and clean way to travel that has been in use for about two centuries. The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed the day in 2018 to recognise the bicycle's value for health, the environment and getting around. Cities and cycling groups mark it with mass rides, car-free streets, bike repair workshops and campaigns for safer cycle lanes, and many people simply ride to work.

National Egg Day on June 3 celebrates one of the most versatile ingredients in the kitchen. Eggs bind, thicken, leaven and emulsify, which makes them essential to everything from omelettes and cakes to mayonnaise, and they are an affordable source of protein. In the United States their reputation got a boost in 1977, when the American Egg Board launched its famous "Incredible, Edible Egg" campaign. Celebrate with a favourite egg dish, whether boiled, scrambled, fried or baked into something sweet.

World Environment Day on 5 June is the United Nations' main day for encouraging awareness and action to protect the environment. The UN General Assembly created it in 1972, choosing the opening day of the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment, and it was first celebrated in 1974 under the theme Only One Earth. Each year the UN Environment Programme picks a theme and a host country, from plastic pollution to land restoration. Millions take part through tree planting, clean-ups, school projects and pledges to live more sustainably.

slogans.en: Land restoration, desertification and drought resilience.

descriptions.en: Constitution Day (Grundlovsdag) on 5 June marks the day in 1849 when King Frederick VII signed Denmark's first democratic constitution, ending absolute monarchy. Later constitutions were also signed on 5 June, including the 1915 version that gave women the vote and the 1953 version still in force today. Danes mark the day with flags, open-air political meetings and speeches across the country, and many workplaces close for the afternoon. It is also Father's Day in Denmark.

Sweden's National Day on 6 June recalls two events: the election of Gustav Vasa as king on 6 June 1523, which laid the foundation of the modern Swedish state, and the adoption of a new constitution on the same date in 1809. It was long celebrated as Swedish Flag Day, became the National Day in 1983 and a public holiday only in 2005. The royal family joins celebrations at Skansen in Stockholm, and towns across the country hold ceremonies welcoming new citizens. Flags fly everywhere.

slogans.en: För Sverige i Tiden! (For Sweden, with the Times!)

descriptions.en: Russian Language Day on 6 June celebrates Russian, one of the six official languages of the United Nations. The UN introduced it in 2010 as part of a series of days honouring each of its official languages, and chose the birthday of Alexander Pushkin, born on this date in 1799, whose poetry and prose shaped the modern literary language. Russia has also marked the day officially since 2011. Readings of Pushkin's verse, literary events, exhibitions and language classes take place wherever Russian is spoken or studied.

slogans.en: The Language of Pushkin Lives On.

descriptions.en: World Food Safety Day, held every 7 June, is a reminder that the food on our plates should never make us ill. The United Nations General Assembly created the day in 2018, and the World Health Organization and the Food and Agriculture Organization have led it since the first observance in 2019. The WHO estimates that around 600 million people fall ill from contaminated food every year. The day is marked with campaigns on safe cooking, clean water and hygiene, from farms and markets to home kitchens.

slogans.en: Food safety: prepare for the unexpected.

descriptions.en: World Chocolate Ice Cream Day falls on 7 June and celebrates one of the best-loved ice cream flavours on the planet. Nobody knows exactly who started it, but the idea is simple: chocolate and ice cream together have been a summer favourite for generations. People mark it by visiting their local ice cream shop, trying a new chocolate variety or making a batch at home. It is also an easy excuse to share a cone with friends as the warm days arrive.

slogans.en: Life is Short, Eat Chocolate Ice Cream!

descriptions.en: World Ocean Day is an annual day of ocean celebration and action. The ocean covers more than 70% of our planet and produces at least 50% of the Earth's oxygen. It is home to most of Earth's biodiversity and is a main source of food and medicine for over 3 billion people.

slogans.en: One ocean, one climate, one future — together.

descriptions.en: National Best Friends Day, marked in the United States on 8 June, celebrates the friend who knows you best. Who started it is unclear, but the reason is easy to understand: a close friend stands by us through laughter, tears and everything in between. People mark the day by calling or meeting their best friend, looking through old photos or simply saying thank you. Many also post tributes on social media to the person who has always had their back.

slogans.en: Side by side or miles apart, best friends are always close at heart.

descriptions.en: National Cancer Thriver Day, observed in the United States on 8 June, honours people who have faced cancer and go on to live with strength, purpose and hope. The word 'thriver' is chosen on purpose: the day is about more than surviving and celebrates an active, meaningful life during and after treatment. People mark it by sharing their stories, supporting friends and relatives touched by cancer and backing organisations that help patients. It is also a chance to remind others that a diagnosis is not the end of a full life.

Portugal Day, on 10 June, is Portugal's national day and a public holiday; its full name is the Day of Portugal, of Camões and of the Portuguese Communities. The date marks the death in 1580 of Luís de Camões, the country's greatest poet and author of the epic 'Os Lusíadas'. The day celebrates the Portuguese language and culture and the many Portuguese people living around the world. It is marked with official ceremonies and military parades, along with concerts, festivals and gatherings in Portuguese communities abroad.

World Games Day on 10 June invites people of all ages to put everything else aside and play. Board games, card games, video games and outdoor games all count, because play is one of the oldest ways people have of having fun together. Games bring people around the same table, sharpen the mind and teach us to win and lose gracefully. People mark the day with family game nights, tournaments among friends or by teaching a favourite game to someone new.

The International Day of Play is observed every 11 June to highlight how vital play is for children's development, health and happiness. The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed it in 2024, and it was celebrated for the first time that year. The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child recognises play as a right of every child, yet many children have little time or safe space for it. The day is marked with games in schools, parks and streets, and with calls to protect children's time to play.

slogans.en: Play is the Language of Children

descriptions.en: National Making Life Beautiful Day, marked in the United States on 11 June, celebrates beauty in all its forms. That can mean art and creativity, but also a kind word, a tidy home or time spent with the people we love. The day encourages small, intentional steps to make our surroundings, our relationships and our inner lives a little richer. People mark it by planting flowers, making something by hand, doing someone a kindness or simply pausing to enjoy what is already beautiful around them.

The World Day Against Child Labour, held every 12 June, draws attention to the millions of children who work instead of learning and playing, many of them in dangerous jobs. The International Labour Organization launched the day in 2002 to rally governments, employers, workers and families against the practice. Each year it carries a theme, and schools, unions and charities mark it with campaigns, talks and events that defend every child's right to education and a safe childhood.

slogans.en: Social justice for all. End child labour.

descriptions.en: Russia Day, on 12 June, is one of the country's main public holidays. It marks 12 June 1990, when the parliament of the Russian Soviet republic adopted the Declaration of State Sovereignty, a key step towards Russia's emergence as an independent state as the Soviet Union came apart. A holiday since 1992, it took its present name in 2002 and is marked with state awards at the Kremlin, concerts, flags and fireworks in cities across the country.

Philippines Independence Day, on 12 June, is the country's national day. It marks 12 June 1898, when General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed independence from Spanish rule at his home in Kawit, Cavite, where the Philippine flag was publicly unfurled and the national anthem was played for the first time. Filipinos celebrate with flag-raising ceremonies, parades, a speech by the president and festivities at home and in Filipino communities abroad.

Democracy Day is a public holiday in Nigeria held on 12 June. It recalls the presidential election of 12 June 1993, widely regarded as the country's freest and fairest, which the military government annulled before the result was declared, although Moshood Abiola was widely believed to have won. Since 2019 the date has replaced 29 May as Democracy Day, and Nigerians mark it with a presidential address, ceremonies and reflection on all who struggled for civilian rule.

slogans.en: The people's choice, the nation's voice.

descriptions.en: World Blood Donor Day, on 14 June, thanks the voluntary, unpaid donors whose blood saves lives every day and reminds everyone that safe blood is always needed. The World Health Organization and its partners started the day in 2004; the date is the birthday of Karl Landsteiner, who discovered the ABO blood groups. Hospitals and blood services mark it with donation drives, thank-you events and campaigns that encourage new donors to give regularly.

slogans.en: Giving blood is an act of solidarity.

descriptions.en: World Juggling Day celebrates the art of keeping several objects in the air at once, one of the oldest skills of circus and street performance. The International Jugglers' Association promotes the day so that jugglers around the world meet, perform and teach in public places. Clubs host open sessions, shows and workshops where beginners try their first throws with balls, rings or clubs, and experienced jugglers share their tricks.

slogans.en: Keep the Balls in the Air!

descriptions.en: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day, on 15 June, highlights the physical, emotional, financial and sexual abuse and neglect that many older people suffer, often at the hands of people they trust. The International Network for the Prevention of Elder Abuse launched the day in 2006, and the United Nations General Assembly formally recognised it in 2011. Organisations mark it with information campaigns, talks and purple ribbons, urging everyone to notice the signs and protect the dignity of older people.

slogans.en: Lift Your Voice Against Elder Abuse.

descriptions.en: World Wind Day, held every 15 June, celebrates the wind as a clean, renewable source of power. It grew out of a European Wind Day and is now promoted worldwide by the wind energy industry, led by WindEurope and the Global Wind Energy Council. Wind farms open their gates, schools run kite and turbine workshops, and families get to see up close how moving air becomes electricity for homes and towns.

World Sea Turtle Day, on 16 June, celebrates reptiles whose ancestors have swum the oceans for more than 100 million years. The date marks the birthday of Archie Carr, the American biologist often called the father of sea turtle conservation. Most of the seven species are now threatened by plastic, fishing nets, lost nesting beaches and warming seas, so aquariums and volunteers hold beach clean-ups, nest patrols and talks on how to protect them.

Bloomsday, on 16 June, celebrates James Joyce's novel Ulysses, which follows Leopold Bloom through a single day in Dublin: 16 June 1904. Joyce reportedly chose the date because it was the day of his first outing with Nora Barnacle, his future wife. Since writers first retraced Bloom's route in 1954, fans in Dublin and around the world dress in Edwardian clothes, read the book aloud, eat Bloom's breakfast and walk the streets he wandered.

slogans.en: Walking through Dublin with Leopold Bloom.

descriptions.en: Youth Day, a public holiday in South Africa on 16 June, remembers the Soweto Uprising of 1976. That morning thousands of Black schoolchildren marched against being forced to learn in Afrikaans, and police opened fire; among those killed was 13-year-old Hector Pieterson, whose photograph shocked the world. Today South Africans mark the day with memorial services, youth events, concerts and visits to the Hector Pieterson Museum in Soweto, honouring young people's role in ending apartheid.

names.en: World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought

descriptions.en: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought, on 17 June, draws attention to fertile land turning to dust through overuse, deforestation and a changing climate. The UN chose the date because the Convention to Combat Desertification was adopted on 17 June 1994, and the day has been observed since 1995. Each year has a theme, and communities plant trees, restore soil and share ways to farm and use water so that land stays healthy for future generations.

slogans.en: United for land. Our legacy. Our future.

descriptions.en: Iceland's National Day, on 17 June, marks the founding of the Republic of Iceland in 1944, when the country ended its union with the Danish crown. The date is the birthday of Jón Sigurðsson, the 19th-century leader of the independence movement. Towns across the country hold parades, brass bands and children's entertainment, and in Reykjavík the Fjallkona, the Lady of the Mountain in national costume, recites a poem to the crowd.

International Picnic Day celebrates the simple joy of sharing a meal outdoors with friends and family. Whether in a local park, a countryside meadow, or your own backyard, the day invites people to slow down, connect, and enjoy nature's dining room. Pack a basket, spread a blanket, and savor the al fresco life.

slogans.en: Pack a basket, share the joy.

descriptions.en: World Sickle Cell Day, on June 19, raises awareness of sickle cell disease, one of the most common inherited blood disorders in the world. In people with the disease, red blood cells take a stiff crescent shape that blocks blood flow, causing anaemia, severe pain and organ damage. The UN General Assembly recognised it as a public health problem in 2008, and the day has been observed since 2009. Health groups use it to promote screening, newborn testing and better access to care, especially in Africa, India and the Mediterranean.

World Sauntering Day, on June 19, invites everyone to slow down and take an unhurried walk. To saunter is to stroll with no goal and no stopwatch, simply enjoying the air, the streets and whatever catches your eye. In a life of deadlines and step counts, the day is a reminder that walking can be a pleasure rather than a task. Mark it by leaving your phone in your pocket and wandering through a park, along the shore or around your neighbourhood.

slogans.en: Slow Down and Smell the Roses

descriptions.en: Juneteenth, on June 19, marks the end of slavery in the United States. On that day in 1865, Union troops reached Galveston, Texas, and announced that the enslaved people there were free, two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation. Black communities have celebrated the date ever since, and in 2021 it became a federal holiday. People mark it with parades, family cookouts, readings of the emancipation order, music and reflection on freedom.

World Refugee Day, on June 20, honours people forced to flee their homes because of war, persecution or violence. The UN General Assembly established it in 2000, and it was first held in 2001, the 50th anniversary of the 1951 Refugee Convention. The day celebrates the courage and resilience of refugees and calls on the world to protect them and help them rebuild their lives. Events include exhibitions, films, shared meals and gatherings that bring refugees and their new neighbours together.

Argentina Flag Day, or Día de la Bandera, is a national holiday on June 20 honouring the flag and the man who created it, Manuel Belgrano. A leader of the independence struggle, Belgrano first raised the light blue and white flag in 1812 on the banks of the Paraná River near Rosario, and he died on June 20, 1820. The main ceremony takes place at the National Flag Memorial in Rosario. Across the country, schoolchildren pledge loyalty to the flag and homes and streets are decked in blue and white.

slogans.en: Honoring the Blue and White — Viva Argentina!

descriptions.en: The International Day of Yoga, on June 21, celebrates a practice of body, breath and mind that began in ancient India. India proposed the day at the United Nations in 2014, the General Assembly adopted it that December, and it was first observed in 2015. The date is the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. People mark it with free group sessions in parks, squares and beaches, where beginners and seasoned practitioners roll out their mats side by side.

names.en: World Music Day (Fête de la Musique)

descriptions.en: World Music Day, known in France as the Fête de la Musique, is held every June 21, on the summer solstice. It began in France in 1982 with a simple idea: anyone, amateur or professional, should be free to play music in public on the longest day of the year. The idea has since spread to cities around the world, where streets, parks and squares fill with free concerts open to everyone.

World Giraffe Day falls on June 21, the longest day of the year in the northern hemisphere, to honour the tallest animal on Earth. It was started by the Giraffe Conservation Foundation to draw attention to giraffes, whose numbers in the wild have fallen sharply in recent decades. Zoos, schools and conservation groups mark it with talks, fundraisers and lessons about the threats giraffes face, from habitat loss to poaching.

Midsommar is the Nordic celebration of midsummer, when the days are at their longest and the nights barely grow dark. In Sweden it is one of the biggest holidays of the year, held on the Friday and Saturday between 19 and 26 June, and Finland and Norway have their own midsummer traditions with bonfires by the water. Swedes raise a flower-decked maypole and dance around it, wear crowns of wild flowers and gather for pickled herring, new potatoes and strawberries. Many spend the weekend outdoors at summer cottages with family and friends.

slogans.en: Dancing Around the Maypole — Welcome Summer!

descriptions.en: The International Day of Yoga is held every June 21 to celebrate yoga, the ancient practice of body, breath and mind that comes from India. India proposed the day to the United Nations, and the General Assembly declared it in 2014; it was first marked in 2015. Each year people gather in parks, studios and public squares for group sessions, and many simply roll out a mat at home to join in.

World Rainforest Day on June 22 celebrates the world's rainforests and the life they sustain. These forests, from the Amazon to the Congo Basin and Southeast Asia, shelter a huge share of the planet's plants and animals, store vast amounts of carbon and shape rainfall far beyond their borders, yet they are still being cleared for farming, logging and mining. People mark the day by learning about rainforests, supporting groups that protect them and choosing products that don't drive deforestation.

National Kissing Day on June 22 is a light-hearted celebration of the kiss in all its forms: romantic, friendly and family. Kissing is one of the oldest and most universal ways people show love, comfort and greeting, though its meaning changes from culture to culture. People mark the day by giving a partner, child or parent an extra kiss, and by sharing favourite kisses from films, art and old photos.

International Being You Day celebrates authenticity and the courage to be your true self. In a world full of expectations about how to look, think and live, it is easy to hide the parts of ourselves that do not fit in. The day is a reminder that each person's quirks, views and ways of being are worth embracing, and that others deserve the same freedom. People mark it by doing something that feels truly their own, sharing what makes them unique, and thanking the friends who accept them as they are.

Olympic Day on June 23 marks the founding of the International Olympic Committee in Paris on June 23, 1894. First held in 1948, it invites people of every age and ability to get moving, whether or not they are athletes. National Olympic committees around the world organise runs, sports taster sessions and school events, often with Olympians taking part, to share the Olympic values of excellence, friendship and respect.

St. John's Eve, the night of June 23, opens the feast of the birth of John the Baptist, one of the few saints celebrated on his birthday rather than the day of his death. Falling close to the summer solstice, it absorbed much older midsummer customs and became one of Europe's best-loved folk festivals. In Spain, Portugal, Norway, Denmark, Latin America and elsewhere people light bonfires, jump over the flames, gather herbs and bathe in the sea or dew for luck.

slogans.en: Jump the bonfire — let the midsummer magic begin.

descriptions.en: International Women in Engineering Day on June 23 celebrates the work of women engineers and encourages more girls to consider a career in engineering. It was launched in the UK in 2014 by the Women's Engineering Society and has since grown into a worldwide observance. Universities, companies and schools mark it by sharing the stories of women engineers, holding talks and workshops, and showing young people the range of jobs engineering offers.

slogans.en: Women build the future — one breakthrough at a time.

descriptions.en: International Widows Day on June 23 draws attention to the women who lose their husbands and, in many countries, also lose their home, income, inheritance or place in society. It was started by the Loomba Foundation, a British charity, and recognised by the United Nations in 2010; the date was chosen because the founder's mother was widowed on June 23. Charities, governments and communities use the day to campaign for widows' rights and to support widows and their children.

Cat World Domination Day on June 24 is a playful celebration of cats' quiet control over their households — and possibly the world. Cats don't ask for power; they already have it. Give your feline overlord the worship they deserve.

slogans.en: Their silence speaks louder than barking ever could.

descriptions.en: Swim a Lap Day, on June 24, is a simple invitation to get into the water and swim at least one length of the pool. Swimming works the whole body while going easy on the joints, which makes it one of the few sports people can keep up at almost any age. Some people use the day to return to the pool after a long break, others to take a first lesson or bring the family along for a summer swim.

slogans.en: One lap. All the benefits. Jump in.

names.en: International Day of Women in Diplomacy

descriptions.en: The International Day of Women in Diplomacy, on June 24, recognises the women who represent their countries abroad, negotiate agreements and work for peace. The UN General Assembly proclaimed the day in 2022, noting that women remain under-represented in diplomacy, especially in senior posts and peace talks. Foreign ministries, embassies and universities mark it with panels, talks and stories of women diplomats, past and present, and with a look at what still stands in the way of equal participation.

slogans.en: Women at the table build peace that lasts.

descriptions.en: World Fairy Day on June 24, close to Midsummer, celebrates the fairies, sprites and other enchanted beings that have filled folklore across many cultures for centuries. From Irish tales of changelings and the Scandinavian älvor to Shakespeare's Titania in A Midsummer Night's Dream and the fairy paintings of the Victorian era, these figures sit on the line between the everyday and the magical. The day invites people to read fairy tales, spend time in nature, build tiny fairy doors and let a little wonder in.

slogans.en: Believe in a little magic today.

descriptions.en: The International Day of the Seafarer, on June 25, thanks the men and women who crew the world's merchant ships and carry most of the goods we use every day. The International Maritime Organization created the day in 2010 and it was first observed in 2011. Each year the IMO picks a theme, often seafarers' welfare, safety or fair treatment, and shipping companies, ports and maritime schools join in with messages of thanks, events and campaigns that remind the public of life at sea, months away from home.

slogans.en: The world moves because they do.

descriptions.en: Global Beatles Day on June 25 celebrates the music and lasting influence of the Beatles, the Liverpool band that changed popular music in the 1960s. The date recalls June 25, 1967, when they performed "All You Need Is Love" on Our World, the first live global television broadcast linked by satellite, seen by an estimated 400 million people. The song's message of peace and love is at the heart of the day. Fans mark it by playing the records, singing along, gathering at tribute concerts and sharing what the band means to them.

World Drug Day, officially the International Day against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, is observed by the United Nations on June 26. The UN General Assembly established it in 1987 to strengthen global cooperation against drug abuse and the illegal drug trade. Each year around this date the UN Office on Drugs and Crime releases its World Drug Report, while health workers, schools and community groups hold awareness events focused on prevention, treatment and support for people affected by drug use.

slogans.en: People First: Stop Stigma and Discrimination.

descriptions.en: National Beauticians Day, on June 26, honours the people who look after our hair, skin, nails and makeup: hairstylists, colourists, estheticians, nail technicians and makeup artists. Their work blends artistry with real technical training, and a good appointment can lift someone's whole week. Caring for appearance is one of the oldest crafts there is, and today it is a skilled, licensed profession in many countries. Mark the day by thanking your stylist, leaving a kind review or booking a little time for yourself.

slogans.en: Beauty is their craft. Confidence is their gift.

descriptions.en: Cancer Wellness Awareness Day on June 26 is a reminder that caring for someone with cancer means more than treating the disease. Alongside medical care, gentle exercise, good food, emotional support and time with others can ease fatigue and stress and help people feel like themselves again. The day speaks to patients, survivors and the families and friends who stand beside them. Wellness centres and support groups mark it with open classes, talks and gatherings, and many people simply reach out to someone going through treatment.

slogans.en: Wellness is not a luxury — it's part of the cure.

descriptions.en: National Chocolate Pudding Day on June 26 celebrates one of America's most beloved comfort desserts. Chocolate pudding's story stretches from 18th-century baked custards to Alfred Bird's egg-free custard powder in 1837 and the first boxed pudding mix from My-T-Fine in 1918. Today it comes in endless forms — classic milk chocolate, dark, white, mint — topped with whipped cream, caramel, or sprinkles. Creamy, nostalgic, and endlessly customizable.

June 26 marks the day in 1960 when British Somaliland, in the north, became independent from Britain. Five days later, on July 1, it united with the former Italian-administered territory in the south to form the Somali Republic, so the two dates are celebrated as a pair. Somalis at home and across the diaspora raise the blue flag with its white star, hold parades and gatherings, and share songs and poems that recall the struggle for independence.

Micro-, Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Day falls on 27 June and was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in 2017. It recognises the corner shops, family workshops, farms and start-ups that make up the great majority of businesses worldwide and provide a large share of jobs. The day is marked with talks, trade events and campaigns on how small firms can get finance, go digital and reach new markets, and it is a good moment to buy from a local business.

names.en: Industrial Workers of the World Day

descriptions.en: Industrial Workers of the World Day on June 27 marks the founding of the IWW in Chicago in 1905 — the union that pioneered 'industrial unionism,' organizing all workers across an entire industry rather than dividing them by trade. Famous for the rallying cry 'an injury to one is an injury to all,' the IWW shaped modern labor through landmark struggles like the 1912 Lawrence Textile Strike. The day honors both that history and the often-invisible industrial work that keeps society running today.

slogans.en: An injury to one is an injury to all.

descriptions.en: Djibouti Independence Day marks 27 June 1977, when the small country on the Horn of Africa became independent from France. Before that it was a French territory, known in its final years as the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas, and a referendum held earlier in 1977 opened the way to independence. The day is celebrated with flag-raising ceremonies, parades, music and public festivities, above all in the capital, Djibouti City.

Happy Heart Hugs Day on 28 June is about the people who make your heart happy but live too far away for a real embrace. Its origin is unclear, yet the idea is simple: distance should not stop warmth from reaching the people we love. People mark it by calling a faraway friend, sending a message or a handwritten card, or sharing a photo that says the hug is waiting for the next time you meet.

slogans.en: Distance can't stop a heart full of love.

descriptions.en: Christopher Street Day takes its name from the street in New York where the Stonewall Inn stands, and where LGBTQ+ people resisted a police raid on 28 June 1969. That uprising became a turning point for the gay liberation movement. In Germany, Switzerland and Austria, Christopher Street Day, or CSD, is the name for Pride events, held in many cities across the summer rather than on a single date. They combine colourful parades, music and street parties with calls for equal rights and visibility.

slogans.en: Pride, visibility, and equal rights for all.

descriptions.en: International Body Piercing Day celebrates body modification as a form of self-expression and personal identity. It honors Jim Ward, often called the granddaddy of the modern piercing movement, who pioneered techniques in the Western world. From ancient tribal traditions to today's studios, the day encourages people to explore piercing as a meaningful way to express individuality.

slogans.en: Express yourself, one piercing at a time.

descriptions.en: Log Cabin Day, held on the last Sunday of June, celebrates the log cabin as a symbol of pioneer life in the United States. Built from felled trees with simple tools, these homes sheltered many settler families and stand today as reminders of hard work and craftsmanship. The day has its roots in Michigan, and historical societies, parks and museums mark it by opening cabins to visitors, demonstrating traditional skills and working to preserve the cabins that survive.

slogans.en: Honoring the pioneering spirit, one log at a time.

descriptions.en: Insurance Awareness Day, observed annually on June 28, encourages people to review their coverage, learn about policy options, and protect their homes, cars, health, and loved ones. It serves as a reminder that coverage needs change over time. Insurance has ancient roots, appearing in the Code of Hammurabi and evolving into modern property insurance after the Great Fire of London in 1666.

slogans.en: Review, protect, and plan for peace of mind.

descriptions.en: The International Day of the Tropics is held on 29 June, a date set by the United Nations General Assembly in 2016. It marks the anniversary of the first State of the Tropics report, published in 2014. The tropics, the broad belt around the equator, are home to rainforests, coral reefs and a large share of the world's plants, animals and people, but they also face poverty, deforestation and the effects of climate change. The day invites everyone to learn about these regions and support their sustainable future.

World Industrial Design Day celebrates the designers who shape the objects we use every day, from chairs and kettles to phones and trams. It was launched in 2007 by the organisation now called the World Design Organization, marking 50 years since its founding on 29 June 1957. Design schools, studios and museums mark the day with exhibitions, talks and open workshops that show how good design makes life safer, simpler and more sustainable.

Hug Holiday on 29 June is a reminder of how much a warm, welcome hug can mean. A hug can comfort, reassure and say what words sometimes cannot, yet many people, especially those living alone and older people in care, can go a long time without friendly touch. People mark the day by hugging family and friends, always with their consent, visiting someone who may be lonely, or simply offering a little extra kindness.

slogans.en: A warm hug heals more than words.

descriptions.en: St. Peter's Day honors one of Jesus' closest followers and the first leader of the Church, celebrating his journey from fisherman to bold spiritual leader. Christians mark it with worship services, coastal blessings, and community gatherings, with especially grand ceremonies in Rome. The feast dates to early Christian Rome and was in religious calendars by the fourth century.

slogans.en: From fisherman to the rock of faith.

descriptions.en: International Fisherman Day on 29 June honours the women and men who make their living from the sea, lakes and rivers. The date is the feast of Saint Peter, a fisherman by trade and the patron saint of fishers, and in many coastal towns it is celebrated with blessings of the boats, sea processions and fish feasts. The day also draws attention to the hard and often dangerous work of small-scale fishers and to the need to fish responsibly so that the seas stay rich for future generations.

slogans.en: Honoring those who feed the world from the sea.

descriptions.en: Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and the only Grand Slam still played on grass. It was first held in 1877 by the All England Club in south-west London, with 22 men in a single event; women's singles followed in 1884. Over two weeks from late June into July, players follow a strict all-white dress code, fans queue for tickets and eat strawberries and cream, and members of the British royal family are often seen in the Royal Box.

slogans.en: Grass, grit, and glory on Centre Court.

descriptions.en: Social Media Day, on 30 June, celebrates how social platforms have changed the way we talk, share news and stay in touch. It was launched in 2010 by the digital media site Mashable to recognise social media's impact on global communication. People mark it by reconnecting with old friends, sharing favourite moments online, joining meet-ups, and taking a moment to think about using social media kindly and responsibly.

National Outfit-of-the-Day Day, on June 30, celebrates personal style and the confidence that comes from wearing a look you love. It takes its name from #OOTD, the hashtag fashion bloggers and social media users made popular for sharing what they wear each day. The point is not expensive clothes but self-expression, whether that means a bold colour, a vintage find or a clever way to restyle something you already own. Mark the day by putting together an outfit that makes you feel good and, if you like, sharing it.

slogans.en: Style it your way, own the day.

descriptions.en: World Snorkeling Day celebrates one of the most accessible ways to explore the underwater world—just a mask, a tube, and fins turn the ocean into a living window. Snorkelers can watch reefs, fish, and turtles up close without the training scuba demands. Emerging through travel communities in the mid-2010s, it also champions ocean awareness and reef protection.

National Meteor Watch Day celebrates the science and wonder of shooting stars—bright streaks made as meteoroids burn up in Earth's atmosphere. It invites people to look up, learn, and share the night sky with loved ones. The date echoes the 1908 Tunguska event, a massive blast believed to be caused by a meteoroid that flattened millions of trees.

slogans.en: Look up and make a wish.

descriptions.en: Queer Youth of Faith Day supports LGBTQ+ young people who want to keep both their faith and who they are. It was started in the United States by the nonprofit Beloved Arise, which works with queer youth across religious traditions. Many of these young people hear that they must choose between their community of faith and themselves; the day says they do not. Congregations, families and friends mark it by sharing stories, offering welcome and showing young people that they belong.

Wildland Firefighter Week of Remembrance, held June 30 to July 6, honors the wildland firefighters who lost their lives battling wildfires. It asks us to remember them by their names and stories, not as statistics. Established in 2014, the week spans the anniversaries of the 2013 Yarnell Hill Fire, which claimed nineteen Granite Mountain Hotshots, and the 1994 South Canyon Fire.

Canada Day, on 1 July, is Canada's national holiday. It marks Confederation in 1867, when the British North America Act joined the Province of Canada, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick into one country; the day was called Dominion Day until 1982. Canadians celebrate with flags, red-and-white clothing, parades, concerts, citizenship ceremonies and fireworks, with the largest gathering on Parliament Hill in Ottawa.

slogans.en: O Canada! True North Strong and Free.

descriptions.en: International Reggae Day (July 1) celebrates reggae music originating from Jamaica in the 1960s. Reggae is recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. Its messages of peace, love, and social justice resonate worldwide.

Maritime and Cabotage Day, on 1 July, celebrates Türkiye's sovereignty over its own coastal waters. On this date in 1926 the Cabotage Law (No. 815) came into force, reserving shipping, trade and port services along Turkish coasts for Turkish citizens and Turkish-flagged vessels, and ending privileges foreign ships had held since Ottoman times. Ports and coastal towns mark it with ceremonies, sounding ship horns, decorated boats, sailing and swimming races, and wreaths laid on the sea.

International Joke Day celebrates humor and laughter by encouraging people to share jokes with friends, family, and even strangers. It highlights the health benefits of laughter, from lower stress to a brighter mood. Jokes have ancient roots—the Greeks recorded some of the first and even hosted early comedy gatherings.

slogans.en: Share a laugh, brighten someone's day.

descriptions.en: National Financial Freedom Day encourages people to pursue financial independence through smart money management, budgeting, and investing. It champions the idea of letting your savings and investments do the heavy lifting so you can live life on your own terms. The day is a yearly reminder to review goals, build good habits, and work toward freedom from financial stress.

slogans.en: Make your money work for you.

descriptions.en: July Morning is a beloved Bulgarian tradition where thousands gather at the coast and in the mountains to welcome the first sunrise of July. More than dawn-watching, it symbolizes freedom, hope, and fresh starts, mixing rock music, camping, and community. It began in the late 1970s as a quiet act of defiance under communism and took its name from a British rock anthem.

slogans.en: Greet the dawn, embrace the freedom.

descriptions.en: Sweetness Week (Semana de la Dulzura) is a much-loved Argentine tradition held July 1–7, when people give a sweet or candy in exchange for a kiss. It started in 1989 as a candy-brand marketing campaign and grew into a nationwide celebration of affection, friendship, and small gestures. Across the week, friends, couples, and coworkers swap treats and kisses to share a little sweetness.

slogans.en: A sweet for a kiss, all week long.

descriptions.en: National Picnic Month, celebrated throughout July, invites everyone outdoors to share meals in nature during the warm summer days. It honors the simple joy of gathering with family and friends in parks and green spaces to eat, relax, and make memories. The word "picnic" dates back centuries, and the tradition has united people from family outings to historic mass gatherings.

National Ice Cream Month celebrates America's favorite frozen treat throughout the hottest month of the year. It encourages enjoying ice cream in every form—cones, bowls, sundaes, and pairings with pie or brownies. The designation was made official by President Ronald Reagan and the American Dairy Association, turning a sweet indulgence into a month-long national celebration.

slogans.en: Scoop up summer, one cone at a time.

descriptions.en: National Anti-Boredom Month, observed in July, is dedicated to beating the summer slump that often follows the Independence Day excitement. It encourages people of all ages to try new hobbies, volunteer, and seek out fresh experiences that stimulate the mind and body. Created by Alan Caruba in the 1980s, it also celebrates how a little boredom can spark creativity and new ideas.

HKSAR Establishment Day, on 1 July, is a public holiday in Hong Kong. It marks the 1997 transfer of Hong Kong from British to Chinese sovereignty and the founding of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under the "One Country, Two Systems" principle. The day opens with a flag-raising ceremony at Golden Bauhinia Square, followed by an official reception, and many residents simply enjoy the summer holiday with family and friends.

World UFO Day invites people to look up at the sky and wonder whether we are alone in the universe. The 2 July date is linked to the 1947 Roswell incident in New Mexico, when debris found on a ranch sparked one of the most famous UFO stories of all time; some groups mark the day on 24 June instead. Fans celebrate with sky-watching parties, science fiction films, talks on the search for life beyond Earth and alien-themed costumes.

slogans.en: Look Up. The Truth is Out There.

descriptions.en: The Palio di Siena is a centuries-old horse race run twice each summer, on 2 July and 16 August, in the shell-shaped Piazza del Campo in Siena, Italy. Ten of the city's seventeen contrade, or neighbourhoods, take part in each race, with jockeys riding bareback for three laps that last about a minute and a half. Days of processions, flag-throwing, trial runs and street dinners lead up to it, and the winning contrada celebrates for weeks.

slogans.en: Siena's heartbeat — the thunder of hooves.

descriptions.en: Made In The USA Day celebrates goods made in the United States and the factories, workshops and workers behind them. Falling just before Independence Day, it invites shoppers to look at the label and think about where their purchases come from. In the US, a product may only claim to be "Made in USA" if all or virtually all of it is made there, a rule enforced by the Federal Trade Commission. People mark the day by buying from local makers and sharing favourite American-made brands.

Thirsty Thursday, on the first Thursday in July, is all about enjoying favorite beverages and socializing with friends as an early start to the weekend. The term originated in Minor League Baseball, coined in 1983 by Ron McKee of the Asheville Tourists. It spread through college culture and into workplaces as people embraced a little midweek merriment.

slogans.en: Cheers to an early start on the weekend.

descriptions.en: World Sports Journalists Day honors the reporters who turn sporting events into compelling stories that bring fans closer to the action. Sports journalists do more than share scores—they shape how we see the game through coverage, analysis, and features. It was established in 1994 to mark the 70th anniversary of the International Sports Press Association (AIPS), founded at the 1924 Paris Olympics.

slogans.en: Bringing the game to life, story by story.

descriptions.en: National Disco Day celebrates the vibrant grooves and inclusive spirit of disco music and culture, inviting everyone to dance and dress in retro style. Disco emerged in the late 1960s from underground clubs serving Black, Latino, and LGBTQ+ communities in New York, where DJs blended soul, funk, and Latin sounds. The day itself began in 2014, created by New Zealand music fans to honor disco's lasting cultural impact.

slogans.en: Put on your dancing shoes and groove.

descriptions.en: International Plastic Bag Free Day asks people everywhere to say no to single-use plastic bags, if only for one day. Bags that are used for a few minutes can last for centuries, breaking into fragments that end up in rivers, seas and the stomachs of animals. People mark the day by carrying a cloth bag or basket, refusing bags at the till, joining clean-ups and pressing shops and local councils to cut plastic waste.

slogans.en: Refuse the bag. Rescue the planet.

names.en: National Stay Out of the Sun Day

descriptions.en: National Stay Out of the Sun Day encourages people to give their skin a break by staying indoors or seeking shade. It raises awareness of UV damage, which can cause sunburn, premature aging, and skin cancer—one of the most common cancers in young adults. The day is a practical reminder to enjoy summer safely with shade, cover-ups, and sunscreen.

slogans.en: Give your skin a break today.

descriptions.en: National Eat Your Beans Day celebrates one of humanity's oldest and most nutritious foods, encouraging people to explore the huge variety of beans enjoyed around the world. Rich in fiber, protein, and minerals, beans have been a staple across nearly every culture for thousands of years. Cultivated beans date back to the seventh millennium BC—even predating pottery.

St. Thomas Day honors Thomas the Apostle, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus, remembered both as "Doubting Thomas" and as a bold missionary said to have carried Christianity as far as India. Marked on July 3rd in the Western Christian calendar, the feast is celebrated with worship and, in many communities, special traditions. It invites reflection on faith, doubt, and conviction.

National Independent Beer Run Day falls on the eve of the Fourth of July and nudges Americans to buy their holiday beer from small, independent breweries. It is promoted by the Brewers Association, the trade group for America's craft brewers, and plays on the idea of celebrating independence with independently made beer. Fans mark it by picking up a six-pack or growler from a local brewery or bottle shop and sharing it at July Fourth cookouts.

Independence Day, the Fourth of July, is the national holiday of the United States. It marks 4 July 1776, when the Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence, announcing that the thirteen American colonies were breaking away from British rule. Americans celebrate with fireworks after dark, parades, flags, backyard barbecues, concerts and family gatherings, and towns large and small hold public readings and patriotic events.

slogans.en: Land of the free, home of the brave.

descriptions.en: Independence From Meat Day invites people to skip meat for a day and discover the benefits of vegetarian and vegan eating. Founded by the Vegetarian Awareness Network in Knoxville, Tennessee, it falls on July 4th to offer a plant-based contrast to America's biggest grilling holiday. It spotlights the health and environmental case for cutting back on meat, from greenhouse gases to water and land use.

slogans.en: One day, no meat, all the flavor.

descriptions.en: The International Day of Cooperatives, held on the first Saturday in July, celebrates how cooperatives improve the lives of their members and communities by blending economic success with social responsibility. The modern movement began in 1844 with English textile workers, and the International Cooperative Alliance has marked this day since 1927. The UN officially recognized it in 1992.

The Tour de France is one of the world's most prestigious cycling races, a test of human endurance across France's dramatic landscapes. Founded in 1903, the first edition covered six stages and about 2,428 km, won by Maurice Garin. Today it spans 21 stages and over 3,500 km—from flat sprints to punishing mountain climbs—captivating fans every July.

slogans.en: Endurance, glory, and the yellow jersey.

descriptions.en: Pet Remembrance Day is a gentle day for remembering the animals we have loved and lost. For many people a dog, cat, rabbit or horse is part of the family, and grief for them can be as deep as any other, even if it is not always acknowledged. People mark the day by lighting a candle, looking through old photos, sharing stories of their pets, visiting a favourite walk or planting a flower in their memory.

slogans.en: Their pawprints stay on our hearts forever.

descriptions.en: National Bikini Day marks 5 July 1946, when the French engineer Louis Réard unveiled his daring two-piece swimsuit at a Paris swimming pool. He named it after Bikini Atoll in the Pacific, where atomic bomb tests had just begun, hoping the design would cause an equally explosive stir. The bikini was shocking at first and banned on some beaches, but it went on to become a summer staple, and today people celebrate with beach days, pool parties and photos in their favourite swimwear.

slogans.en: Sun, sand, and the freedom to shine.

descriptions.en: National Workaholics Day is a reminder to step back from excessive work and value work-life balance. It acknowledges that while hard work matters, rest, relationships, and time away from the job are essential to well-being. The term "workaholic" was coined around the 1940s, and the day highlights the body and mind's genuine need for balance.

Algeria celebrates its independence from France on 5 July, the day it was proclaimed in 1962 after a war of liberation that began in November 1954. The date was chosen with care: French troops had entered Algiers on 5 July 1830, so the holiday closes 132 years of colonial rule on the same day it began. Known as Independence and Youth Day, it is marked with flag-raising ceremonies, parades, concerts and fireworks, as families honour those who died in the struggle.

National Fried Chicken Day celebrates one of the world's most beloved comfort foods, enjoyed at restaurants, home kitchens, and gatherings alike. Fried chicken has ancient roots—it appears in Roman cookbooks—but took its iconic form in America through a blend of Scottish and West African traditions. Once a delicacy, it became a global staple after the Second World War.

slogans.en: Crispy, golden, and impossible to resist.

descriptions.en: International Kissing Day celebrates the affection expressed through kissing—romantic, familial, and friendly alike. It grew out of British National Kissing Day, established around 2005–2006, before spreading worldwide. While kissing has ancient roots noted in texts dating to 1500 BC, this modern day recognizes its role in human connection, always with respect for consent and cultural boundaries.

slogans.en: Share a kiss, spread the love.

descriptions.en: National Transplant Week, held in the UK in early July, raises awareness of how organ donation saves and transforms lives and encourages people to register their decision. A single donor can help several people, and thousands across the UK are waiting for a kidney, liver, heart or other organ at any time. Every part of the UK now treats adults as willing donors unless they opt out, but families are still consulted, so telling your loved ones what you want matters. NHS Blood and Transplant now runs its main campaign as Organ Donation Week in September.

Comoros Independence Day marks 6 July 1975, when the Comoros declared independence from France. Three of the archipelago's four main islands, Grande Comore, Anjouan and Mohéli, formed the new state, while Mayotte remained under French administration, which the Comoros still contests. The national holiday is celebrated with flag-raising, official speeches, parades and music and dancing across the islands, as families gather for festive meals.

World Chocolate Day, celebrated on 7 July, is a cheerful excuse to enjoy one of the world's best-loved treats. Chocolate comes from the seeds of the cacao tree, which the peoples of Mesoamerica, including the Maya and the Aztecs, prepared as a bitter, spiced drink long before it reached Europe in the 16th century. Over the centuries Europeans sweetened it and turned it into the bars, pralines and hot chocolate we know today. People mark the day by sharing their favourite chocolate, baking a chocolate cake or trying a new bar from a local chocolatier.

National Dive Bar Day celebrates the beloved subculture of dive bars—no-frills spots known for cheap drinks, jukeboxes, and unpretentious charm. Founded in 2018 by Seagram's Seven Crown to support historic preservation, it recognizes these neighborhood haunts as genuine cultural spaces. The July 7th date nods to the lucky number seven tied to the brand.

slogans.en: Cheap drinks, good company, no pretense.

descriptions.en: Global Forgiveness Day encourages people to let go of grudges and anger and to forgive those who have wronged them. Established in 1994 by CECA in Canada, it has grown into a worldwide observance centered on healing and reconciliation. The day reminds us that releasing resentment can free the mind and mend relationships.

The National Day of Rock 'n' Roll honors the genre's huge influence on culture and society. Rock 'n' roll didn't just shape music—it broke down social barriers and helped drive major cultural shifts, giving the world icons like Elvis Presley and The Beatles. Established by Christina Alexander in 2020, the day invites people to celebrate through listening, live performances, and sharing favorite tracks.

slogans.en: Turn it up and rock on.

names.en: National Father Daughter Take a Walk Day
