descriptions.en: National Father Daughter Take a Walk Day encourages dads to spend meaningful one-on-one time with their daughters through a simple walk and shared conversation. It recognizes that daughters of every age benefit from their father's time and attention. Emerging in the 1970s as gender roles evolved, the day continues to promote strong father-daughter bonds across all stages of life.

International Peace & Love Day falls on 7 July, Ringo Starr's birthday, and invites everyone to spread a little more kindness. It began in 2008, when the former Beatles drummer was asked what he wanted for his birthday and answered simply: "peace and love." Each year fans around the world pause at noon local time, flash the peace sign and say the words together. Others mark it with small acts of care: a call to an old friend, a kind word or a helping hand.

slogans.en: Peace and love, pass it on.

descriptions.en: World Change Day is dedicated to personal and social transformation, built on the idea that lasting change begins with each individual. It is a prompt to pause and ask what you would like to do differently, whether that is a habit, a relationship, or the way you treat the people and places around you. People mark the day with meditation and yoga sessions, community gatherings, volunteering and small personal commitments that can grow into bigger change over time.

Tell the Truth Day challenges people to spend a whole day being honest in both words and actions. Studies suggest most people tell only one or two lies a day, yet even small, convenient untruths can wear away trust over time. The day invites you to notice the moments when a white lie feels easier, to set the record straight on something you have been avoiding, and to have the kind of open, kind and honest conversation that strengthens relationships.

slogans.en: Just for today, only the truth.

descriptions.en: The Running of the Bulls is a thrilling Spanish tradition where bulls charge through narrow streets as daring runners sprint alongside them. It traces back to the 14th century, when farmers moved bulls to market and young men began running with them to show courage. By the 16th century it became part of Pamplona's San Fermín festival, now a globally famous event held each July.

National Video Game Day, on July 8, celebrates video games and the huge place they now hold in culture, from early arcade cabinets and home consoles to PC, mobile and online play. It is easily confused with Video Games Day on September 12, and many fans happily celebrate both. Games tell stories, train quick thinking and bring friends and families together across a room or across the world. Mark the day by replaying an old favourite, trying a new genre or inviting someone who has never played to join in.

Be a Kid Again Day encourages adults to reconnect with their inner child through play, curiosity, and simple delights. As George Bernard Shaw put it, "we don't stop playing because we grow old; we grow old because we stop playing." Founded in 1990 by Atari creator Nolan Bushnell, it's a yearly nudge to swap stress for wonder.

World Allergy Day draws attention to allergic diseases such as hay fever, asthma, eczema and food allergies, which affect a large and growing share of people around the world. Allergies can range from a mild nuisance to a life-threatening reaction, and many people live for years without a proper diagnosis. The day encourages people to learn their triggers, see a doctor about persistent symptoms, and know how to respond to a severe reaction, while doctors and patient groups share advice on prevention and care.

Math 2.0 Day celebrates the bond between mathematics and modern technology. Behind every search engine, weather forecast, bank transfer and medical scan sits mathematics, often invisible to the people who rely on it. The day invites us to see maths not as a school chore but as the quiet engine of the digital world. Mark it by trying a puzzle, exploring a coding or data project, or showing a young person where the maths they learn turns up in everyday life.

Argentina Independence Day, on 9 July, is one of the country's most important national holidays. On this day in 1816, the Congress of Tucumán declared the independence of the United Provinces of South America from the Spanish crown, in a house in San Miguel de Tucumán that is now a national museum. Argentines celebrate with flags, parades, official ceremonies and folk music. Families and friends gather around traditional dishes such as locro, a hearty stew, along with empanadas and sweet pastelitos.

Fashion Day celebrates personal style and the creativity of expressing yourself through what you wear. Rather than following the season's trends or the big fashion houses, it puts the focus on individual taste, whether that means a bold outfit, a vintage find or a well-loved accessory. Clothing has always said something about who we are, where we come from and how we want to be seen. People mark the day by dressing up, sharing their looks online, swapping clothes with friends or giving old pieces a new life.

names.en: Don't Step On A Bee Day

descriptions.en: Don't Step On A Bee Day reminds us to protect bees from accidental harm and to support their conservation. It highlights the vital role bees play in pollination and food production. Founded by Ruth and Thomas Roy, it has grown alongside global concern over declining bee populations, which have dropped sharply in some regions in recent decades.

slogans.en: Watch your step, save a bee.

descriptions.en: National Kitten Day celebrates kittens and raises awareness for the many that need rescue and homes. Founded in 2012 by pet behaviorist Colleen Paige, it encourages adoption, volunteering, and donations to cat charities. Moved from December to July to align with peak kitten season, it also promotes spaying and neutering to ease overpopulation.

World Kebab Day, on the second Friday in July, celebrates the beloved grilled meat and vegetable dish on skewers that unites culinary traditions across the globe. Kebabs originated in the Middle East and spread along trade routes through Central Asia, giving rise to favorites like shish and doner. The day invites restaurant visits, barbecues, and creative homemade kebabs.

Global Energy Independence Day encourages the world to embrace alternative energy sources like solar, wind, and geothermal power. First celebrated in 2005 and founded by green-energy advocate Michael D. Antonovich, it falls on July 10th to honor inventor Nikola Tesla's birthday and his early renewable-energy vision. The day promotes reducing dependence on fossil fuels and building a sustainable future.

slogans.en: Power the future, break the dependence.

descriptions.en: Chronic Disease Awareness Day works to increase public understanding of chronic conditions and improve access to health information. Founded by the nonprofit Good Days and observed since around 2017, it educates people about prevention, early detection, and available resources. The July 10th date underscores that chronic illness drives seven of the top ten leading causes of death in the US.

World Population Day is an annual event observed every July 11 to raise awareness about global population issues. The world's population reached 5 billion on July 11, 1987. Today, we are over 8 billion people.

All-American Pet Photo Day encourages pet owners to snap photos of their companions and share them online. It celebrates the joy pets bring and the special bond between people and their animals. With no documented founder, it has grown into a beloved annual tradition that inspires pet lovers to capture their animals' unique personalities.

slogans.en: Snap it, share it, love your pet.

descriptions.en: World Rum Day celebrates rum, the spirit distilled from sugarcane juice or molasses, together with the people who make, mix and enjoy it. Rum took shape on the sugar plantations of the Caribbean in the 17th century, a history bound up with colonial trade and slavery, and it travelled the world with sailors and merchants. In early colonial New South Wales it was even used as a form of currency. Today bars and distilleries mark the day with tastings, classic cocktails and talks on rum's long and complicated story.

slogans.en: Raise a glass to the spirit of sugarcane.

descriptions.en: National Swimming Pool Day celebrates the simple joy of swimming and cooling off in the summer heat. It encourages people to visit local pools, splash around, and enjoy time with friends and family. First celebrated in 2016, it builds on a long history of swimming—from ancient Roman baths to the sport's modern revival after the 1896 Olympic Games.

names.en: National Cheer Up the Lonely Day

descriptions.en: National Cheer Up the Lonely Day encourages people to reach out to those feeling isolated through simple acts of kindness—a call, a visit, or a kind word. Founded by Francis Pesek of Detroit, it aims to combat the loneliness so many experience, especially those who are homebound or in care. The July 11th date marks his birthday and his lifelong spirit of compassion.

slogans.en: A small kindness can light up a day.

descriptions.en: Malala Day, on July 12, honours Malala Yousafzai and the right of every girl to go to school. Malala spoke out for girls' education in Pakistan's Swat Valley and survived being shot by the Taliban in 2012. On her 16th birthday in 2013 she addressed the United Nations in New York, and Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon declared the day Malala Day. A year later, at 17, she became the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate. People mark it by speaking up and supporting girls' schooling.

slogans.en: One child, one teacher, one book, one pen can change the world.

descriptions.en: Barn Day, held in July, celebrates the barn as the heart of the family farm: the place for animals, hay, tools and the work that keeps a farm running. Many old barns are now disappearing, and with them a piece of rural history and craftsmanship, so the day invites people to notice and value the ones still standing. Farms and local groups mark it with open days, barn tours and community gatherings, and photographers and painters head out to capture weathered red barns in the summer light.

slogans.en: Where community, heritage, and hard work meet.

descriptions.en: World Circle Dance Day celebrates rhythmic, synchronized movement that connects people across the globe, integrating body, mind, heart, and spirit. Though circle dancing is an ancient practice, the modern movement began in 1970s Scotland as a way of centering retreat participants. Established in 2016, it now brings together over 250 groups from more than 25 countries.

Paper Bag Day celebrates the humble, versatile paper bag and its role as an eco-friendly alternative to plastic. It honors the innovations that made it a daily essential—Charles Stilwell's 1852 bag-making machine and his 1883 square-bottom design, later improved with handles by Margaret Knight and Walter Deubener. The day encourages creative reuse and more sustainable packaging.

National Simplicity Day honors the birthday of Henry David Thoreau and celebrates the idea that living with less can bring greater happiness. It invites people to declutter their lives and minds—reading, spending time in nature, and unplugging from technology. Thoreau's two years at Walden Pond remain a timeless reminder to focus on what truly matters.

World Day of Rock Music, on 13 July, marks the anniversary of Live Aid, the 1985 benefit concert held at the same time in London and Philadelphia to raise money for famine relief in Ethiopia. Organised by Bob Geldof and Midge Ure, it brought together many of the biggest names in rock and was watched on television around the world. The day is especially popular in Brazil, where it is known as Dia Mundial do Rock. Fans celebrate with concerts, radio specials and their favourite albums played loud.

slogans.en: Rock On! Music Unites the World.

descriptions.en: International Rock Day celebrates rocks and stones—the naturally occurring aggregates of minerals that literally form the ground beneath us. It recognizes their vital role in human history, from Stone Age tools to the metals and minerals that power modern life. The day invites curiosity about geology and the story the Earth tells through its rocks.

Embrace Your Geekness Day encourages everyone to proudly show off their passions—comics, sci-fi, gaming, tech, and every niche hobby in between. Created by Wellcat Holidays (Tom and Ruth Roy), it celebrates how being a geek has shifted from an insult to a badge of honor. The day is all about owning what you love and the creativity it sparks.

slogans.en: Own your passions, geek out proudly.

descriptions.en: The Galway International Arts Festival transforms the Irish city into a two-week hub of theatre, music, dance, and visual art each July, drawing hundreds of thousands of visitors. Performances spill from theatres into public squares and streets. Founded in 1978 by artists including Ollie Jennings and Bill Whelan, it has grown into one of Europe's leading arts events.

slogans.en: Two weeks of art fills Galway.

descriptions.en: Bastille Day is the French National Day, celebrated on 14 July each year. In France it is called La Fête Nationale. It commemorates the Storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789, which was a turning point in the French Revolution.

World Chimpanzee Day on 14 July celebrates chimpanzees, our closest living relatives, who share nearly all of our DNA and live in complex, tool-using communities. The date recalls 14 July 1960, when Jane Goodall arrived at Gombe in Tanzania to begin her landmark study of wild chimpanzees. Today the species is endangered by habitat loss, disease and the illegal bushmeat and pet trade, so the day is marked with talks, zoo and sanctuary events and fundraising for conservation across Africa.

slogans.en: Our closest cousins need our help.

descriptions.en: Cow Appreciation Day, on the second Tuesday in July, celebrates cows and their contributions to food and agriculture. It began in 1995 as a playful Chick-fil-A campaign built around cows urging people to "Eat Mor Chikin." The quirky idea grew into an annual tradition where fans dress up as cows for fun and free food at participating restaurants.

slogans.en: Moo-ve over and celebrate the cows.

descriptions.en: International Non-Binary People's Day celebrates people whose gender identities exist beyond the traditional male/female binary. Founded in 2012 by Katje van Loon, its date sits halfway between International Women's Day and International Men's Day, symbolizing the space in between. The day aims to raise awareness, challenge discrimination, and build community for non-binary people worldwide.

Iraq Republic Day on 14 July marks the 1958 revolution that ended the Hashemite monarchy and proclaimed the Republic of Iraq. Led by army officers under Abd al-Karim Qasim, the uprising overthrew King Faisal II and set the country on a new political path. The date remains one of the defining turning points of modern Iraqi history, and it is marked as a public holiday with official ceremonies, flags and speeches recalling the birth of the republic.

slogans.en: The monarchy ended, the republic began.

descriptions.en: Democracy and National Unity Day commemorates the defeat of the coup attempt on the night of July 15–16, 2016. Citizens took to the streets in response to President Erdoğan's call, and the attempt was repelled by the early hours of July 16. The day became a public holiday in 2017 to honour those who lost their lives defending democracy and to remember the night Turkey resisted a military takeover.

slogans.en: Democracy is the voice of the people.

descriptions.en: National Pet Fire Safety Day encourages pet owners to make safety plans and fire-proof their homes to protect their animals. Around 500,000 pets are affected by home fires each year, making prevention and preparedness essential. Established in 2009 by the American Kennel Club and ADT Security Services, it highlights both the risks pets face and hazards they can accidentally create.

National Clean Beauty Day celebrates cosmetics made with natural, organic ingredients that are kinder to skin and the environment. Founded in 2020 by Juice Beauty to mark its 15th anniversary, it raises awareness of the clean beauty movement and encourages safer, more sustainable choices. It reflects the idea that what we put on our skin matters as much as what we put in our bodies.

World Youth Skills Day, on July 15, highlights how much young people's futures depend on the skills they gain for work and life. The UN General Assembly declared the day in December 2014, and it was first observed in 2015. Because young people are far more likely than adults to be out of work, the day champions technical and vocational education, apprenticeships and training that help them find jobs or start their own businesses. Schools, training centres and governments use it to showcase young people's talents and to discuss what still needs to change.

Social Media Giving Day, on July 15, invites people to use their online accounts for something more than scrolling: supporting a cause they care about. Charities increasingly raise money and awareness through social networks, where a single post can reach friends, family and strangers within minutes. People mark the day by donating, starting or sharing a fundraiser, or posting about an organisation whose work matters to them, ideally after checking that the charity is genuine before they give.

National I Love Horses Day celebrates humanity's deep, ancient bond with horses, domesticated for roughly 6,000 years. From transportation and farm work to sport and companionship, horses have shaped cultures across the world. The day honors their strength, grace, and loyalty—and invites horse lovers to spend time with these remarkable animals.

slogans.en: Grace, strength, and a loyal heart.

descriptions.en: Arctic Sea Ice Day, created by Polar Bears International, raises awareness of the rapid decline of Arctic sea ice. This vital frozen landscape sustains polar bears and marine life and helps regulate the global climate. The day calls for education and action to slow ice loss driven by a warming planet, reminding us that the far north's ice affects us all.

slogans.en: Save the ice, save the Arctic.

descriptions.en: National Respect Canada Day encourages Canadians to appreciate and honor the country's rich cultural mosaic. Established in 2014, it promotes inclusivity, unity, and mutual respect across communities. The day is a reminder to treat everyone with dignity, regardless of background, and to celebrate the diversity that shapes Canadian life.

slogans.en: Unity in diversity, respect for all.

descriptions.en: National Give Something Away Day, on July 15, encourages people to pass on things they no longer need to someone who can use them. It can be clothes, books, toys or household items, but also time, a skill or a simple kind gesture. Giving helps the person who receives and often lifts the giver's mood too, and it keeps useful things out of the bin. Mark the day by clearing a shelf or wardrobe and donating to a neighbour, a charity or a local swap group.

slogans.en: Give a little, brighten a lot.

descriptions.en: Saint Swithin's Day commemorates a humble 9th-century Bishop of Winchester known for his charity. English folklore holds that the weather on this day sets the pattern for the next 40 days: "St Swithin's day if thou dost rain, for forty days it will remain." The tradition blends faith, legend, and a bit of meteorological superstition into an enduring English custom.

Celebration of the Horse Day honors the deep bond between people and horses—built on trust, steady movement, and quiet understanding—and their role in healing, teaching, and bringing communities together. While the U.S. Senate established a December National Day of the Horse in 2004, this informal summer celebration grew organically to let people gather outdoors and honor horses through learning and connection.

World Snake Day on 16 July is dedicated to one of the most misunderstood animals on Earth. Snakes live on every continent except Antarctica and play a vital role in nature, keeping rodent numbers in check and serving as food for birds of prey and other animals. The day aims to replace fear with understanding: zoos, wildlife centres and schools hold talks and safe encounters, while conservation groups highlight the many species threatened by habitat loss and persecution.

The Fiesta de la Tirana transforms the small northern Chilean town of La Tirana into a dazzling blend of faith and culture, drawing tens of thousands to honor the Virgen del Carmen. Held around July 16th, it bursts with traditional dances, music, and elaborate costumes. Legend says it began with an indigenous princess who converted to Christianity, and Spanish missionaries later wove local traditions into Catholic devotion.

National Cherry Day celebrates the sweet, jewel-red fruit of summer, enjoyed fresh, baked, or preserved. It encourages cherry picking, festivals, and baking, from pies to preserves. Cherries originated in Asia Minor, were spread by the Greeks and Romans, and reached America with English colonists in the 1600s.

slogans.en: Life is just a bowl of cherries.

descriptions.en: National Personal Chef Day, on July 16, honours the professionals who cook in clients' own kitchens, planning menus around a household's tastes, diets and schedules. It was created by the American Personal & Private Chef Association to bring attention to this young corner of the food trade. The day also nods to everyone who feeds the people they love at home. Mark it by thanking a cook in your life, trying a new recipe for someone, or learning how personal chefs work.

Artificial Intelligence Appreciation Day celebrates how AI quietly improves daily life — from navigation and smart assistants to healthcare diagnostics — while stressing fair, ethical, and responsible design. Founded in 2021 by A.I. Heart LLC, it invites open conversations about AI's real-world impact and its future role in society.

World Emoji Day is an annual event on July 17 celebrating emoji. The date was chosen because it is the date displayed on the Calendar emoji in iOS. With over 3,600 emoji currently in the Unicode Standard, emojis have become a universal language.

The World Day for International Justice highlights the global fight against war crimes, genocide, and crimes against humanity, and the pursuit of accountability for victims. It marks the adoption of the Rome Statute in 1998, which created the International Criminal Court as a permanent institution. The day promotes justice, human rights, and the rule of law worldwide.

National Tattoo Day celebrates the rich history and artistry of tattoos as forms of self-expression. Tattoos have ancient roots — Ötzi the Iceman bore them 5,000 years ago — and appear across cultures from Egypt and China to Polynesia. The day honors that heritage, celebrates modern tattoo artists, and challenges lingering stigma around body art.

slogans.en: Ink your story on your skin.

descriptions.en: Gentse Feesten is one of Europe's largest cultural festivals — ten days of music, theatre, street performance, and food filling the historic heart of Ghent, Belgium. It began in 1843 as a city-organized community celebration and grew over generations into a massive, joyful summer institution. Despite wartime interruptions, it has always returned stronger.

slogans.en: Ten days of music, joy, and Ghent.

descriptions.en: Nelson Mandela International Day is held every 18 July, Mandela's birthday, to honour the anti-apartheid leader who became South Africa's first democratically elected president. The United Nations declared the day in 2009, and it was first observed in 2010. People are invited to give 67 minutes of their time to helping others, one minute for each of the 67 years Mandela spent in public service, through volunteering, clean-ups, food drives and other acts of community service.

The Drina Regatta is one of the region's largest water festivals, a joyful non-competitive float down Serbia's scenic Drina River from Perućac to Rogačica. Boats are decorated in vibrant colors amid music, dancing, and local food. Established in 1994 in Bajina Bašta, it honors the legacy of the river's traditional raftsmen and now draws thousands of visitors each summer.

The International Snowdon Race is a punishing mountain run up and down Snowdon (Yr Wyddfa), Wales's highest peak, over a 15.35 km course from Llanberis. Held on the third Saturday in July, it draws elite fell runners from around the world. It began in 1976 when Ken Jones wondered how fast someone could run up and down the mountain — 86 runners took the first challenge.

slogans.en: Up the mountain and back — if you can.

descriptions.en: World Listening Day invites us to truly listen to the world around us — its soundscapes, its acoustic ecology, its quiet and its clamor — not just to one another. Rooted in the World Soundscape Project and first held in 2010, it falls on the birthday of composer R. Murray Schafer, a founder of acoustic ecology. It's a call to notice, and protect, the sounds of our environment.

slogans.en: Listen to the world around you.

descriptions.en: Perfect Family Day celebrates family bonds through simple, meaningful time together — a shared meal, a game, an outdoor adventure. Established in 1999, it grew from a wish to help people slow down and reconnect. Its message is gentle and inclusive: whatever your family looks like, time spent together is what makes it perfect.

The Festival of Archaeology invites people across the UK to explore the nation's heritage through digs, tours, workshops, and talks, making the distant past feel vivid and hands-on. It runs for a fortnight each July to coincide with peak fieldwork season. Organised by the Council for British Archaeology, it began in 1990 as National Archaeology Day with just ten activities.

World Ice Cream Day celebrates one of the world's best-loved treats, in the middle of the northern summer. It grew out of America's National Ice Cream Day: in 1984 President Ronald Reagan proclaimed July National Ice Cream Month and its third Sunday National Ice Cream Day. Ice cream itself comes in countless forms, from Italian gelato and Turkish dondurma to Indian kulfi and Japanese mochi ice cream. Many ice cream shops mark the day with discounts and new flavours, while people simply treat themselves to their favourite cone.

slogans.en: Life is Short, Eat More Ice Cream.

descriptions.en: World Chess Day on 20 July was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in 2019, which chose the anniversary of FIDE's founding in Paris in 1924. The UN recognised chess as a game that combines sport, science and art, and as a tool for education, fair play and mutual respect between nations. Across the world, the day is celebrated with tournaments, school activities and friendly matches online and in public spaces, where anyone can sit down at a board and play.

Colombia's Independence Day on 20 July recalls the events of 1810 in Santa Fe de Bogotá, when a dispute over a flower vase sparked an uprising and the signing of an act that created a local governing council. This Cry of Independence began the long struggle against Spanish rule, which was decided at the Battle of Boyacá in 1819. Today Colombians mark the day with military parades, concerts, flags in every window and festivities in towns across the country.

International Chess Day falls on 20 July, the date on which the International Chess Federation, FIDE, was founded in Paris in 1924. FIDE has celebrated the day since 1966, and it honours a game whose roots reach back about 1,500 years to India. Clubs, schools and federations around the world mark it with tournaments, simultaneous exhibitions and open games in parks and squares, celebrating chess as a pastime that brings people of every age and background together.

Space Exploration Day on 20 July recalls the day in 1969 when Apollo 11 landed on the Moon, carrying Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin, the first people to walk on its surface. Their mission, watched by hundreds of millions of people on television, showed what science, engineering and teamwork could achieve. The day celebrates human curiosity and the drive to explore beyond our planet, and it is marked with planetarium shows, stargazing nights, museum events and lessons on space science.

slogans.en: One small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.

descriptions.en: Moon Day celebrates humanity's first lunar landing on July 20, 1969, when Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon during Apollo 11. It honors one of history's greatest feats of exploration and engineering. Established in the US in 1971 and designated International Moon Day by the UN in 2021, it reflects on our ongoing journey into space.

slogans.en: One small step, one giant leap.

descriptions.en: Friend's Day (Día del Amigo) is a beloved Argentine celebration of friendship, when people fill cafés and homes to toast the bonds they share. It was inspired by the 1969 Apollo 11 Moon landing — dentist Enrique Febbraro saw humanity's shared achievement as proof friendship could unite the world. Officially recognized in 1979, it's now one of Argentina's most social days.

slogans.en: Here's to friends, near and far.

descriptions.en: National Lollipop Day celebrates the cheerful candy on a stick that has brightened childhoods for generations. People have long eaten sweets and candied fruit on sticks, but the hard candy lollipop we know took off in the early 20th century, when machines made it cheap to produce, and the Bradley Smith Company trademarked the name "Lolly Pop" in the early 1930s. Mark the day by enjoying a lollipop in your favourite flavour or sharing a few with friends and children.

slogans.en: Sweeten your day, one lick at a time.

descriptions.en: World Jump Day is a playful, tongue-in-cheek event inviting people worldwide to jump at the same moment — originally an art project claiming a synchronized leap could nudge Earth's orbit and fight climate change. It's physically impossible, of course, but that's the point: a witty celebration of collective action and global connection. Created by artist Torsten Lauschmann, first held in 2006.

Global Hug Your Kids Day encourages parents to hug their children and cherish the time they have together. Founded in 2008 by Michelle Nichols — a decade after she lost her young son to cancer — it's a tender reminder that childhood passes quickly. It also celebrates the real health benefits of hugs, from lower stress to a stronger heart.

slogans.en: Hug them tight while they're small.

descriptions.en: Belgium's National Day on 21 July recalls the day in 1831 when Leopold I took the constitutional oath as the first King of the Belgians. His accession followed the revolution of 1830, which separated Belgium from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. In Brussels the day is marked with a military and civilian parade before the royal family, a popular festival in the city's parks and an evening fireworks display, while towns across the country hold their own celebrations.

slogans.en: Eendracht maakt macht — Unity is Strength.

descriptions.en: No Pet Store Puppies Day raises awareness of puppy mills and urges people to adopt from shelters instead of buying from pet stores. Many pet-shop puppies come from large breeding facilities that put profit over welfare, keeping dogs in cramped, unhealthy conditions. Launched by the ASPCA in 2011, it champions #AdoptDontShop and humane treatment of animals.

World Collie Day celebrates one of the most intelligent and devoted dog breeds, known for alert eyes, flowing coats, and a calm, loyal nature. Collies originated as herding dogs in Scotland and northern England, rose to fame after Queen Victoria adopted the breed, and became icons through Lassie. The day honors their loyalty and the deep bonds they form with people.

Racial Harmony Day is marked in Singapore on 21 July, the date the 1964 race riots broke out on the island. Singapore began observing it in 1997 so that each generation would remember how fragile peace between communities can be. Schools lead the day: pupils come in traditional Chinese, Malay, Indian and Eurasian dress, play old games and share each other's food, while community groups hold talks and cultural shows.

World Brain Day, on 22 July, is run by the World Federation of Neurology and falls on the anniversary of the federation's founding in 1957. Each year it picks one theme, such as migraine, stroke, epilepsy or brain health across a lifetime, and puts it in front of the public. Neurologists, hospitals and patient groups mark it with talks, free check-ups and campaigns about sleep, exercise and other everyday habits that protect the brain.

Pi Approximation Day celebrates the fraction 22/7, a handy estimate of π (about 3.1429) — hence the date 22/7. A summery, lighter cousin of Pi Day (March 14), it's popular in schools and science centers, with games, food, and puzzles. The approximation dates back over 2,000 years to Archimedes, who used it to bound the value of pi.

Revolution Day on 23 July is Egypt's national day. It recalls the 1952 coup by the Free Officers, led by Muhammad Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser, which forced King Farouk to abdicate and led to the proclamation of the republic the following year. It is a public holiday: the president addresses the nation, official ceremonies are held, and television fills the day with patriotic songs and films about the revolution.

World Whale and Dolphin Day on 23 July celebrates the ocean's great mammals, from the blue whale, the largest animal ever known, to the playful dolphins seen off many coasts. Many species are still at risk from fishing nets, ship strikes, underwater noise and polluted water. Aquariums, marine groups and coastal towns mark the day with talks, beach clean-ups and responsible whale-watching trips that show these animals in the wild.

names.en: National Women Touched by Addiction Day

descriptions.en: National Women Touched by Addiction Day honors women who have faced addiction themselves or supported loved ones through recovery. It works to reduce stigma, share stories of resilience, and create compassionate space for healing. Founded in 2021 by Mending Hearts, a Nashville nonprofit, it grew from their mission to house and support women in recovery.

Tisha B'Av is a solemn Jewish day of mourning and fasting, remembering the destruction of both Temples in Jerusalem and other tragedies in Jewish history. Observed on the 9th of Av (July 22–23 in 2026), it involves fasting, reading the Book of Lamentations, and quiet reflection. Its roots stretch back over 2,500 years to the fall of the First Temple in 586 BCE.

slogans.en: A day of mourning and remembrance.

descriptions.en: International Self-Care Day falls on 24 July, a date chosen as a reminder that self-care works 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. It was launched in 2011 by the International Self-Care Foundation to show how much of our health rests on everyday choices: sleep, food, movement, hygiene and knowing when to see a doctor. People mark it by setting aside time for rest and small healthy habits, while pharmacies and health groups share practical advice.

slogans.en: Self care is not selfish — it's essential.

descriptions.en: National Tequila Day toasts the iconic Mexican spirit distilled from blue agave, the star of margaritas and countless cocktails. Tequila's roots run deep — its ancestor pulque was made as early as 150 BC — and true tequila must be at least 51% blue agave from regions like Jalisco. Mexico officially recognized the day in 2018 as a global celebration.

slogans.en: Salt, lime, and a taste of Mexico.

descriptions.en: Pioneer Day is a Utah state holiday marking the arrival of Brigham Young and the first Latter-day Saint pioneers in the Salt Lake Valley on July 24, 1847. It celebrates their westward journey, resilience, and the communities they built. Utahns mark it with parades, rodeos, fireworks, and family gatherings honoring the pioneers' legacy.

World Drowning Prevention Day, held every July 25, was declared by the UN General Assembly in 2021. The World Health Organization estimates that about 300,000 people drowned in 2021, many of them young children, and most in low- and middle-income countries. Nearly all of these deaths can be prevented with simple steps: watching children closely near water, fencing pools and wells, teaching swimming and water safety, and wearing life jackets on boats. Governments, lifeguards and community groups mark the day with safety campaigns and swimming lessons.

National Wine and Cheese Day, celebrated on July 25, honors one of the world's most beloved culinary pairings. The combination of wine and cheese dates back thousands of years, both products sharing a reliance on the science of fermentation and aging. Across the globe, enthusiasts gather for tastings and pairings that highlight regional varieties of wine and artisanal cheeses. Whether a bold red with aged cheddar or a crisp white with brie, this day invites everyone to explore the art of pairing.

National Day of the Cowboy is celebrated on the fourth Saturday of July in the United States, honoring the enduring legacy of the American cowboy. Cowboys played a central role in the development of the American West, herding cattle across vast open ranges and shaping the culture of frontier life. Today the day is marked by rodeos, western festivals, and celebrations of cowboy culture including music, art, and horsemanship. The cowboy spirit of independence, hard work, and freedom continues to inspire people around the world.

Carousel Day celebrates the timeless magic of the carousel, one of the oldest and most beloved amusement rides in history. The modern carousel traces its origins to 17th-century Europe, evolving from equestrian training devices into the ornate spinning rides adorned with hand-carved horses and fantasy animals we know today. On July 25, 1871, the first US patent for a steam-powered carousel was granted, making this date its official anniversary. Carousels continue to delight riders of all ages at amusement parks, boardwalks, and town squares around the world.

slogans.en: Round and round, the magic never stops.

descriptions.en: The Feast of Saint James, celebrated on July 25, honors James the Great, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus and the patron saint of Spain. According to tradition, James was the first apostle to be martyred, beheaded by Herod Agrippa around 44 AD, and his relics are believed to rest at the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela in Spain. The feast is especially significant in Galicia, where Santiago de Compostela serves as the destination of the famous Camino pilgrimage route. Thousands of pilgrims complete the Camino each year, arriving at the cathedral to pay their respects on this holy day.

slogans.en: The way of Saint James leads to grace.

names.en: International Day of Women and Girls of African Descent

descriptions.en: The International Day of Women and Girls of African Descent, observed on July 25, was proclaimed by the United Nations in 2021 to recognize and address the unique forms of discrimination faced by women and girls of African descent worldwide. These women and girls are disproportionately affected by intersecting forms of racism, sexism, and poverty. The day calls on governments and civil society to take concrete steps to eliminate racial discrimination and promote gender equality. It amplifies the voices of African-descendant women in politics, culture, science, and the arts.

slogans.en: Their voices rise, their strength endures.

descriptions.en: National Marine Week, observed in late July in the United Kingdom, is an annual celebration organized by The Wildlife Trusts to highlight the rich biodiversity of Britain's seas and coastlines. The event encourages people to discover, explore, and protect the marine environment through rockpooling, guided snorkeling, and beach clean-ups. Britain's seas are home to thousands of species, from seals and dolphins to colorful anemones and starfish. The week raises awareness of the threats facing ocean habitats, including plastic pollution, climate change, and overfishing.

slogans.en: Dive into the blue — our seas need you.

descriptions.en: Republic Day in Tunisia falls on 25 July, the day in 1957 when the Constituent Assembly abolished the monarchy of the beys and proclaimed a republic. Habib Bourguiba, who had led the country to independence the year before, became its first president. The day is a public holiday, marked with flags on public buildings, official ceremonies and cultural events across the country.

slogans.en: The day the republic was declared.

names.en: International Day for the Conservation of the Mangrove Ecosystem

descriptions.en: The International Day for the Conservation of the Mangrove Ecosystem, on 26 July, was proclaimed by UNESCO in 2015. Mangroves are salt-tolerant forests that grow where land meets sea in the tropics; their tangled roots shelter young fish, soften storm surges and lock away large amounts of carbon. Yet they are being cleared for farms, shrimp ponds and building, so the day is marked with replanting drives, guided walks and lessons on why these coastal forests matter.

National Dog Photography Day, celebrated on July 26, is a day for dog lovers and photography enthusiasts to capture their furry friends in all their playful, goofy, and adorable glory. Dogs are among the most photogenic subjects in the world, their expressions and antics making for endlessly joyful images. The day encourages pet owners to pick up their cameras — or smartphones — and document their dogs' unique personalities and favorite moments. From action shots in the park to cozy portraits at home, this day celebrates the unbreakable bond between humans and their canine companions.

Esperanto Day, observed on July 26, commemorates the publication of the first Esperanto textbook on July 26, 1887, by Dr. Ludwik Lazarus Zamenhof. Zamenhof, a Polish ophthalmologist, created Esperanto as a neutral international language intended to foster peace and understanding among people of different nations. Today, Esperanto is spoken by an estimated one to two million people worldwide, making it the most widely spoken constructed language. The day celebrates the enduring vision of a world united by a shared language, free from the barriers that divide us.

names.en: World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly

descriptions.en: The World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly, held on the fourth Sunday of July, was instituted by Pope Francis in 2021 to honor the role of grandparents and elderly people in the life of families and society. The day encourages younger generations to visit and spend time with their grandparents and elderly relatives, combating the epidemic of loneliness that affects many older people. Elderly people carry irreplaceable wisdom, memories, and love that form the foundation of families and communities. The annual theme always centers on the dignity, presence, and invaluable contribution of the elderly.

Love Parks Week, held in late July in the United Kingdom, is an annual campaign celebrating the importance of public parks and green spaces in communities across Britain. Organized by Keep Britain Tidy and other conservation groups, the week encourages people to get outside, enjoy their local parks, and take pride in caring for these shared spaces. Parks play a crucial role in public health and wellbeing, offering free recreational space, nature connection, and community gathering points. Activities include litter picks, nature walks, picnics, and community events that bring neighborhoods together.

slogans.en: Love your park, love your community.

descriptions.en: National Scotch Day celebrates Scotland's centuries-old whisky tradition, honoring the distilling craft passed down since medieval monks first brought spirit-making techniques to the Highlands. What began as a medicinal tonic evolved into the aged, peated spirit prized by drinkers worldwide today. The day invites enthusiasts to sample single malts and blends from Scotland's many storied distilleries.

slogans.en: Raise a glass to Scotland's finest.

descriptions.en: Sleepy Head Day is a centuries-old Finnish tradition that pokes affectionate fun at the last person in the household to wake up. Rooted in medieval legend and moved from June to July in 1709, the custom says late risers will be sluggish for the rest of the year. Families mark it playfully with a splash of water, while the town of Naantali holds a famous public ceremony tossing a celebrity into the sea.

names.en: National Korean War Veterans Armistice Day

descriptions.en: This observance honors the Americans who served in the Korean War, which began on June 25, 1950, when North Korean forces invaded the South. After three years of brutal fighting, an armistice was signed on July 27, 1953, halting active combat and creating the Korean Demilitarized Zone that still divides the peninsula. Often called the "Forgotten War," the day ensures its veterans and their sacrifices are remembered.

names.en: International Safe Places to Work Day

descriptions.en: International Safe Places to Work Day shines a spotlight on workplaces where people feel free to speak up, question, disagree, and be themselves without fear. Founded by the Safe Places to Work initiative, it champions psychological safety alongside physical safety, drawing on research like Google's Project Aristotle, which found that teams perform best when members feel safe to be vulnerable. The day encourages leaders to build trust and openness into everyday culture.

World Hepatitis Day, on 28 July, is one of the World Health Organization's official health days. The date honours the birthday of Baruch Blumberg, the Nobel Prize-winning scientist who discovered the hepatitis B virus and helped develop a vaccine against it. Viral hepatitis inflames the liver and often goes unnoticed for years, so the day is marked with free testing, vaccination drives and campaigns urging people to get checked and treated.

World Swimming Day on July 28 celebrates swimming as both a sport and a life skill. Swimming works the whole body while going easy on the joints, so it suits people of almost any age, and knowing how to swim can save a life in the water. Pools, clubs and swim schools mark the day with open sessions, beginner lessons and water safety tips, and many people simply take a dip in a pool, lake or the sea.

Peru's Independence Day on July 28 marks the day in 1821 when General José de San Martín proclaimed the country's independence from Spain in Lima's main square. It opens Fiestas Patrias, Peru's biggest national holiday, which continues on July 29. Homes and streets are hung with red-and-white flags, the president addresses the nation before Congress, and families gather for parades, music, dancing and traditional food.

World Nature Conservation Day on July 28 is a reminder that a healthy natural world underpins everything we depend on, from clean air and water to food and a stable climate. It calls attention to protecting forests, wildlife, soil and oceans, and to using natural resources wisely so that they last for future generations. Schools, environmental groups and local communities mark it with tree planting, clean-ups, nature walks and talks about living more sustainably.

slogans.en: Conserve Nature for a Better Tomorrow

descriptions.en: National Soccer Day celebrates the beautiful game—a global passion built on skill, teamwork, and the thrill of scoring goals. Established in 1994, it honors the players, coaches, and fans of one of the world's most widely played sports. Soccer's modern rules took shape in 1800s London, though ball games resembling it date back thousands of years.

slogans.en: One ball, one world, endless passion.

descriptions.en: National Milk Chocolate Day celebrates the creamy confection made from cocoa solids blended with dry or condensed milk. Swiss inventor Daniel Peter developed it in the 1870s after his neighbor Henri Nestlé's milk-powder process inspired him to soften dark chocolate's bitterness. His innovation sparked a sweeter alternative that would go on to dominate the global chocolate market. Today, the day is marked with a well-earned bar — or ten.

The King's Birthday on July 28 honours King Maha Vajiralongkorn, Rama X, who was born on this day in 1952. It is a public holiday in Thailand and one of the country's main royal occasions. People wear yellow, the colour linked to the King's day of birth, decorate buildings with his portrait and royal flags, make merit at temples by offering food to monks, and join candle-lighting ceremonies in the evening.

slogans.en: Long live the king, long live Thailand.

descriptions.en: International Tiger Day, also called Global Tiger Day, is held every July 29 to raise awareness of the tiger and the threats it faces. It was agreed at the 2010 Tiger Summit in St. Petersburg, where tiger range countries set the goal of doubling wild tiger numbers. Tigers are listed as Endangered by the IUCN, and a 2022 estimate put the wild population at roughly 3,700 to 5,600, threatened by poaching and habitat loss. Zoos, schools and conservation groups mark the day with talks, campaigns and fundraising.

slogans.en: Saving tigers is saving our planet.

descriptions.en: Global Tiger Day on July 29, also known as International Tiger Day, draws attention to the plight of wild tigers, which have lost most of their historic range to habitat loss and poaching. The day was agreed at the Saint Petersburg Tiger Summit in 2010, where the countries that are home to wild tigers pledged to double their numbers. Zoos, conservation groups and schools mark it with talks, fundraising and campaigns to protect forests and stop the illegal wildlife trade.

National Lipstick Day celebrates one of beauty's most iconic products and its centuries-long history of self-expression. Founded by beauty entrepreneur Huda Kattan in 2016, the day invites people to experiment with bold new shades and celebrate the confidence a swipe of color can bring. From ancient natural pigments to today's endless finishes and formulas, lipstick remains a small, powerful act of personal style.

National Lasagna Day pays tribute to the layered Italian pasta dish that has become a beloved staple in kitchens around the world. Tracing its origins to medieval Naples, lasagna made its way to America in the 19th century and has since taken on countless regional twists — from classic beef and béchamel to vegetarian and seafood variations. The day is best celebrated with a generously layered, bubbling tray straight from the oven.

Rain Day celebrates the quiet, life-giving importance of rainfall to every living thing on Earth. The tradition began in the late 1800s when pharmacist William Allison noticed it rained on July 29 in Waynesburg, Pennsylvania almost every year, a curious pattern that gained worldwide attention in the 1930s thanks to journalist John O'Hara. Today people mark it by learning about rainfall patterns, dancing in a summer shower, or simply appreciating water's role in sustaining life.

slogans.en: Let it pour, let it matter.

descriptions.en: July 29 is the second day of Peru's Fiestas Patrias, the national holiday that begins with Independence Day on July 28. Its highlight is the Great Military Parade in Lima, where the armed forces and police march before the president, watched by large crowds and on television across the country. With two days off in a row, many Peruvians travel or visit family, and towns fill with fairs, folk music, dances such as the marinera and traditional dishes.

The International Day of Friendship on July 30 was proclaimed by the UN General Assembly in 2011. It rests on the idea that friendship between peoples, countries, cultures and individuals can inspire peace and build bridges between communities. The UN encourages governments, schools and community groups to hold events that bring different people together, and many simply use the day to get in touch with old friends, thank them, or reach out to someone new.

slogans.en: Sharing the human spirit through friendship.

descriptions.en: The World Day against Trafficking in Persons on July 30 draws attention to the victims of human trafficking and to the protection of their rights. The UN General Assembly designated the day in 2013, recognising trafficking as a grave crime that exploits women, men and children through forced labour, sexual exploitation and other abuse. UN agencies, governments and charities mark it with awareness campaigns, survivors' stories and calls for stronger action to prevent trafficking and bring traffickers to justice.

slogans.en: Act to Protect. Act to Support.

descriptions.en: Throne Day on July 30 is Morocco's national holiday, marking King Mohammed VI's accession to the throne in 1999 after the death of his father, King Hassan II. The King delivers a televised Throne Speech to the nation, and a ceremony of allegiance is held at which officials and representatives renew their loyalty to the monarch. Across the country, streets are decked with flags and portraits of the King, and towns hold concerts, fireworks and public celebrations.

slogans.en: Long Live His Majesty the King!

descriptions.en: National Cheesecake Day celebrates one of the world's oldest and most beloved desserts, believed to have been invented by the Ancient Greeks around 200 A.D. as one of the first-ever "sweet" treats. First conceived in 1985, the observance took off with the rise of the internet in the early 2000s and is now marked worldwide. People celebrate with everything from classic New York-style slices to fruit-topped, no-bake, and chocolate-swirled variations.

Pol'and'Rock Festival, formerly known as Woodstock Festival Poland, began in 1995 as a free tribute concert honoring volunteers of the Great Orchestra of Christmas Charity. It has since grown into one of Europe's largest non-commercial music festivals, drawing hundreds of thousands of fans to the Polish countryside for days of live music, workshops, and social activism. Founded by Jerzy Owsiak, the festival remains free to all, championing peace, unity, and inclusivity.

World Avocado Day on July 31 celebrates the creamy fruit that has found its way onto plates around the globe. The avocado is native to south-central Mexico, where it was eaten for thousands of years, and Mexico is still by far its largest producer today. Botanically it is a berry with a single large seed. People mark the day by making guacamole, topping toast with smashed avocado, blending it into smoothies or trying it in a dessert.

World Ranger Day on July 31 honours the rangers who protect national parks, wildlife and protected areas, and remembers those killed or injured on duty. It was set up by the International Ranger Federation, which chose the anniversary of its own founding. Rangers patrol remote land, track poachers, fight fires and guide visitors, often at real personal risk. On the day, parks and conservation groups hold memorials, share rangers' stories and raise funds for their families.

National Mutt Day, also marked again each December 2, celebrates mixed-breed dogs and raises awareness of the many wonderful mutts still waiting in shelters. Founded by animal welfare advocate Colleen Paige, the day pushes back against the stigma sometimes attached to the word "mutt," highlighting how these dogs often combine the best traits of multiple breeds. It's a call to adopt, care for, and celebrate every one-of-a-kind mixed-breed companion.

The Flower Fair, known locally as Feria de las Flores, transforms Medellín into a vibrant celebration of floral artistry and Colombian pride. Founded in 1957 by tourism promoter Arturo Uribe as a modest five-day festival with 40 silleteros (flower-carrying farmers), it has grown into a ten-day celebration drawing visitors from around the world. The signature Silleteros Parade sees locals carry towering, elaborate flower arrangements on their backs, alongside music, dance, and food honoring the region's growers.

Swiss National Day on 1 August recalls the founding of the Old Swiss Confederacy in 1291, when the valley communities of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden pledged mutual aid in the Federal Charter. The date was first celebrated nationwide in 1891, for the alliance's 600th anniversary, and became a public holiday across the whole country in 1994. The Swiss mark it with bonfires on hilltops, fireworks, children's lantern processions and speeches in town squares. Many farms open their doors for a festive brunch, and houses and streets are decked with red-and-white flags.

World Wide Web Day on 1 August celebrates the web, the system of linked pages that made the internet usable for everyone. British scientist Tim Berners-Lee proposed it in 1989 while working at CERN, the European physics laboratory near Geneva, and the web opened to the public in 1991. In 1993 CERN released the technology royalty-free, which let the web grow into the shared space we know today. People mark the day by remembering the first websites they visited, learning a little HTML, supporting free online resources or helping someone less familiar with the web get online.

National Fishing Month, celebrated throughout August in the United Kingdom, is an annual initiative that encourages people of all ages to try fishing for the first time or rediscover the sport. Fishing is one of Britain's most popular leisure activities, with millions of anglers enjoying rivers, lakes, canals, and coastal waters each year. The campaign provides free or subsidized fishing sessions to introduce newcomers to the sport, emphasizing the mental health benefits of time spent quietly by the water. The month celebrates fishing as a pursuit that connects people to nature, builds patience, and fosters a love of the outdoors.

slogans.en: Cast a line, catch a memory.

descriptions.en: National Girlfriends Day, observed in the United States on August 1, celebrates friendship between women. It honours the friends who have been there for decades as well as newer ones who have quickly become family. Women's friendships often carry people through big life changes, and the day is a reminder not to take them for granted. People mark it by calling or texting a friend, meeting for brunch or a girls' night out, or sending a card to say thank you.

slogans.en: Celebrate the women who have your back.

descriptions.en: National Spider-Man Day on August 1 celebrates the web-slinging superhero created by writer Stan Lee and artist Steve Ditko. Spider-Man first appeared in Marvel's Amazing Fantasy #15, cover-dated August 1962, as Peter Parker, a teenager from Queens, New York, bitten by a radioactive spider. His everyday struggles and the lesson that great power brings great responsibility made him one of the most loved heroes in comics. Fans mark the day by reading comics, rewatching the films and cartoons, and dressing up in red and blue.

slogans.en: With great power comes a great celebration.

descriptions.en: World Lung Cancer Day on 1 August raises awareness of lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer deaths worldwide. It was set up by international lung health organisations to honour those affected and to push for prevention, earlier diagnosis and better treatment. Smoking is the main cause, but radon, second-hand smoke and air pollution also raise the risk, and people who have never smoked can develop the disease too. On the day, doctors and patient groups share advice on quitting smoking and screening, hospitals hold awareness events, and survivors tell their stories.

International Childfree Day on August 1 recognises people who have chosen not to have children. It matters because this choice is still often met with pressure, pity or prying questions, even though many people build full and meaningful lives without parenthood. The day pushes back on those stereotypes and celebrates the many ways adults contribute to their families, friends and communities. People mark it by sharing their stories, reading and talking about the choice, and simply respecting each person's decision.

Respect for Parents Day, observed in the United States on 1 August, invites people of every age to thank the parents and parent figures who raised them. It matters because the patience, sacrifice and everyday care behind a childhood often go unspoken, and a day set aside makes room to say what usually goes unsaid. People mark it by calling or visiting their parents, sharing a meal, writing a heartfelt note or remembering those who have passed away. Many also extend their thanks to grandparents, step-parents and guardians who stepped into that role.

National Yorkie Day on August 1 celebrates the Yorkshire Terrier, a toy breed with a big personality. The breed was developed in Yorkshire, in northern England, during the 19th century, where small terriers were kept to catch rats in mills and mines before becoming fashionable companions. Yorkies are known for their long, silky coat, bold spirit and loyalty to their owners. Owners mark the day with extra walks, treats and grooming, sharing photos of their dogs and supporting Yorkie rescue groups.

Albariño Day celebrates the crisp, aromatic white grape at home in Galicia, in north-western Spain, above all in the Rías Baixas wine region. Across the border in northern Portugal the same grape is called Alvarinho and grown in the Vinho Verde region. Its wines are known for bright acidity and notes of citrus, peach and a hint of sea salt, which makes them a classic match for seafood. Wine lovers mark the day by opening a chilled bottle, ideally with shellfish or grilled fish.

National Peach Month turns August into a celebration of one of summer's juiciest fruits, at the height of the harvest in the United States. The peach was first cultivated in China thousands of years ago and travelled west along trade routes through Persia, which is why its Latin name, Prunus persica, points to Persia. Today peaches come in yellow and white, freestone and clingstone varieties. People enjoy the month by eating them fresh, grilling them, baking cobblers and pies, or making jam to keep summer in a jar.

Lebanese Army Day on August 1 marks the founding of Lebanon's national army in 1945, when troops that had served under the French Mandate passed to the command of the newly independent Lebanese state. The army is widely seen as one of the few institutions that unites the country across its many communities. The day is marked with official ceremonies, wreath-laying for soldiers killed on duty and the commissioning of new officers graduating from the military academy. Flags and messages of thanks to the troops appear across the country.

National Tree Day, celebrated on the first Sunday of August in Australia, is the country's largest community tree-planting event. Founded in 1996 by Planet Ark, the initiative has seen more than 24 million trees and plants planted by over four million Australians at schools, parks, bushland reserves, and local community spaces. Planting trees is a simple but powerful act for fighting climate change, restoring habitats, and improving local environments. National Tree Day inspires Australians to connect with nature and take tangible action to protect the natural world for future generations.

slogans.en: Plant a tree, grow a future.

descriptions.en: National Ice Cream Sandwich Day on 2 August celebrates the simple pleasure of ice cream pressed between two cookies or soft chocolate wafers. The treat has been an American favourite for well over a century, sold from street carts, corner shops and ice cream trucks, and today it comes in countless variations. People mark the day by picking one up from the freezer aisle, making their own with homemade cookies and favourite flavours, or sharing a box with friends on a hot summer afternoon.

slogans.en: Two cookies, one scoop of joy.

descriptions.en: International Assistance Dog Week, held in the first full week of August, honors the dogs that help people with disabilities live more independently. Guide dogs lead people who are blind, hearing dogs signal sounds such as doorbells and alarms, and other dogs pick up dropped items or warn of seizures and low blood sugar. The week is also a moment to thank the trainers, puppy raisers and volunteers behind every working dog, and to remind everyone not to pet or distract a dog in harness.

National Watermelon Day, on August 3, celebrates one of summer's best-loved fruits. Watermelon was first cultivated in Africa thousands of years ago and is now grown in warm climates around the world; true to its name, it is more than 90 percent water. People mark the day with cold slices at picnics, watermelon salads with feta and mint, fresh juices and the occasional seed-spitting contest.

Stop on Red Week, held in early August, is a road-safety campaign about the dangers of running red lights. Drivers who speed through a red signal cause serious crashes at intersections, often striking pedestrians, cyclists or cars crossing on green. Safety groups and local authorities use the week to share reminders and push for safer intersections, urging every driver to slow down when the light turns yellow and to stop fully on red.

National Chocolate Chip Cookie Day, on August 4, celebrates one of the world's best-loved cookies. The recipe is credited to Ruth Wakefield, who ran the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts and published it in the late 1930s after folding chopped pieces of chocolate into a butter cookie dough. Fans mark the day by baking a fresh batch at home, sharing cookies with friends or coworkers, and debating whether they are best crisp or chewy.

slogans.en: A timeless treat, one chip at a time.

descriptions.en: National White Wine Day, on August 4, celebrates wines made mostly from green-skinned grapes, from crisp Sauvignon Blanc to rich Chardonnay and fragrant Riesling. White wine is usually made by pressing the grapes and separating the juice from the skins before fermentation, which keeps its color pale and its taste fresh. On this summer day, people open a chilled bottle with seafood, salads or light dishes, try a grape they have never tasted, or visit a local winery.

Single Working Women's Day is an American observance that honours women who build their careers and run their households on their own. Single working women carry every bill, decision and deadline alone, and they often face assumptions about their lives that married colleagues do not. People mark the day by thanking a single working friend, sister or colleague, treating her to lunch or a small gift, and simply recognising how much she manages by herself.

International Clouded Leopard Day, on August 4, draws attention to one of Asia's most elusive wild cats. Named for the cloud-shaped blotches on its coat, the clouded leopard lives in forests from the Himalayan foothills to Southeast Asia, is a superb climber and has the longest canine teeth for its size of any living cat. The species is listed as vulnerable, threatened by deforestation and poaching, so zoos and conservation groups use the day to share its story and raise support for protecting its forests.

Assistance Dog Day celebrates the trained dogs that help people with disabilities and medical conditions go about daily life with more freedom. Some guide people who are blind, some alert people who are deaf to important sounds, and others open doors, carry items or warn their owner of an oncoming seizure. Each of them has been through long, careful training, and the day is a chance to thank the dogs, their trainers and handlers, and to learn how to behave around a working dog.

Blogger Day celebrates the people who write blogs, from personal diaries and travel journals to recipe sites and expert guides. Blogging grew out of the early web's online diaries and gave anyone with a keyboard a way to publish their own voice without a newspaper or a publisher. People mark the day by reading and sharing posts from their favourite bloggers, leaving a kind comment, or finally starting the blog they have been putting off.

National Underwear Day is a light-hearted American observance devoted to the garment everyone wears and few people talk about. It began in the 2000s as a retail promotion and grew into a day about comfort, confidence and feeling good in your own skin. People mark it by treating themselves to a fresh pair, clearing out worn-out drawers, or donating new underwear to shelters, where it is one of the most requested and least donated items.

names.en: National Work Like A Dog Day

descriptions.en: National Work Like A Dog Day is an American observance that honours people who put in long hours and give every task their full effort. Its name comes from the old saying about working like a dog, and from the herding, guide, rescue and farm dogs that truly do work hard every day. People mark it by thanking the hardest workers they know, rolling up their sleeves on a tough job, or, just as fairly, remembering to rest afterwards.

International Scuba Day celebrates diving with a self-contained underwater breathing apparatus, the equipment that lets people stay beneath the surface and explore the sea up close. Scuba opened coral reefs, shipwrecks and kelp forests to ordinary divers, and many of them have become committed defenders of the oceans they visit. Divers mark the day by heading out on a dive, joining reef or beach clean-ups, or introducing a friend to the underwater world with a first try-dive.

slogans.en: Dive into a whole new world.

descriptions.en: Balloons to Heaven Day is a day of remembrance for loved ones who have died. Families and friends gather to share memories and write messages to the person they miss, a simple ritual that helps grief feel shared rather than carried alone. Many once released balloons into the sky, but because loose balloons harm wildlife, people now often choose gentler gestures such as planting a tree, blowing bubbles, lighting a candle or visiting a favourite place together.

Jamaica Independence Day marks 6 August 1962, when Jamaica ended more than three centuries of British colonial rule and became an independent nation within the Commonwealth. It comes just days after Emancipation Day on 1 August, which recalls the end of slavery, so Jamaicans celebrate the two together in a week of national pride. The country fills with black, green and gold flags, street parades, church services, reggae and mento music, a grand gala and plenty of jerk chicken.

Aged Care Employee Day is an Australian day of thanks for everyone who works in aged care, not only nurses and carers. It also recognises the cooks, cleaners, gardeners, drivers, activity staff and office teams whose work makes a care home feel like a real home. Residents, families and providers mark it on 7 August with thank-you cards, shared morning teas, small gifts and kind words for the people behind elderly Australians' daily comfort.

slogans.en: The quiet heroes of aged care.

descriptions.en: The Bristol Balloon Fiesta is Europe's largest annual hot air balloon event, held each August at Ashton Court on the edge of Bristol. It began in 1979 and has grown into a free, four-day gathering that draws balloonists from around the world. Crowds gather for the mass ascents at dawn and early evening, when the sky fills with colour, and for the Night Glow, when tethered balloons light up in time to music after dark.

On 7 August 1819, patriot forces led by Simón Bolívar and Francisco de Paula Santander defeated the Spanish royalist army at the bridge over the Teatinos River in Boyacá. The victory opened the road to Bogotá and proved decisive for the independence of New Granada, today's Colombia. The anniversary is a national holiday marked with military parades, flag ceremonies and school events, and it is also the date on which Colombian presidents take office.

International Cat Day on 8 August celebrates cats, companions that have lived alongside people for thousands of years since their domestication in the Near East. The day was created in 2002 by the International Fund for Animal Welfare to raise awareness of cats and how to protect them, and it has been led by the charity International Cat Care since 2020. People mark it by spoiling their own cats, sharing photos online and supporting shelters through donations, fostering or adoption.

Scottish Wildcat Day, on August 8, draws attention to Britain's only native wild cat, nicknamed the 'Highland tiger'. Larger and stockier than a house cat, with a thick, blunt, black-ringed tail, it once roamed much of Britain but now survives only in Scotland, where it is critically endangered. The biggest threat is interbreeding with feral and domestic cats, so the day promotes neutering pets, supporting conservation groups and captive breeding and release programmes.

National Happiness Happens Day, held on August 8, is a reminder that happiness often shows up in small, ordinary moments. It matters because noticing those moments, and sharing them, can lift both our own mood and the mood of the people around us. People mark it by passing on good news, thanking someone, doing a small kindness or simply taking time for something that makes them smile.

slogans.en: Share the joy, spread the happiness.

descriptions.en: National Dollar Day marks August 8, 1786, when the Congress of the young United States set up a national money system built on the dollar. Before that, Americans paid with a confusing mix of colonial currencies and foreign coins, especially Spanish silver dollars. Today the dollar is one of the most widely used currencies in the world, and the day is a chance to look at its history, its familiar green notes and the coins people collect.

slogans.en: A currency, a history, a legacy.

descriptions.en: Digital Nomad Day celebrates people who use the internet to work from anywhere, combining a career with life on the move. Remote work, laptops and fast connections have made it possible to swap a fixed office for cafés, coworking spaces and rented flats in cities around the world, and many countries now offer special visas for remote workers. People mark the day by sharing travel and work tips, meeting fellow nomads, or simply planning their next base.

International Infinity Day falls on 8 August, the eighth day of the eighth month, because the number 8 turned on its side looks like the infinity symbol ∞. That symbol was introduced by the English mathematician John Wallis in 1655, and the idea of the endless has fascinated mathematicians, philosophers, artists and astronomers ever since. People mark the day by exploring puzzles and paradoxes about infinity, making art inspired by the symbol and reflecting on ideas that have no limit.

names.en: International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples

descriptions.en: The International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples is a United Nations observance held every August 9. The UN General Assembly chose the date in 1994 to mark the first meeting of the UN Working Group on Indigenous Populations, held in Geneva in 1982. The day celebrates the languages, knowledge and cultures of Indigenous peoples and highlights their rights to land, identity and self-determination, through UN events, community gatherings, exhibitions and educational programmes.

slogans.en: Indigenous peoples and a new social contract.

descriptions.en: Book Lovers Day, on August 9, is an invitation to set everything else aside and spend time with a good book. It matters because reading opens doors to other lives, places and ideas, and a single book can change how we see the world. People mark it by starting a new book or returning to an old favourite, visiting a library or bookshop, swapping recommendations with friends and giving a book as a gift.

slogans.en: Open a Book, Open Your Mind.

descriptions.en: Singapore's National Day on 9 August marks the city-state's independence in 1965, when it separated from Malaysia after two years as part of the federation. Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew announced the separation that day, and the young nation, with few natural resources, set out to build a multiracial republic. The centrepiece of the celebrations is the National Day Parade, with military displays, performances, flypasts and fireworks, watched live by thousands and on screens by many more. Homes and housing blocks are decked in red-and-white flags for weeks beforehand, and many families watch the parade together.

National Opportunity Day is a reminder that there is more than one road to a fulfilling working life. It speaks especially to students weighing their next step and to adults thinking about a change of career, encouraging them to look beyond the usual school-to-university-to-office track. Apprenticeships, vocational training, learning a trade, starting a business or retraining later in life are all paths worth considering. People mark the day by exploring new options, talking to mentors or simply asking themselves which opportunity they have been putting off.

slogans.en: Every path can lead somewhere great.

descriptions.en: Betty Boop Day falls on August 9, the date in 1930 when the character first appeared on screen in Max Fleischer's cartoon 'Dizzy Dishes'. She began as a side character with doglike features but soon became a human flapper with big eyes, spit curls and the catchphrase 'Boop-Oop-a-Doop', one of the first famous female cartoon stars. Fans mark the day by watching her classic black-and-white shorts, listening to jazz-age songs and dressing up in 1930s style.

International Coworking Day, on August 9, celebrates shared workspaces where freelancers, remote workers and small teams work side by side. The date honours programmer Brad Neuberg, who in 2005 launched what is widely seen as the first coworking space in San Francisco, a place to work independently without working alone. Coworking spaces around the world mark the day with open-door visits, talks, workshops and get-togethers that celebrate community and collaboration.

Hold Hands Day, on August 9, celebrates one of the simplest and most powerful gestures of human connection. Holding hands can calm nerves, offer comfort in hard moments and say 'I'm here' without a single word, whether between partners, parents and children, friends or an older relative. People mark the day by reaching for a loved one's hand on a walk, sitting close with family, or keeping someone company who needs a little support.

slogans.en: A little touch, a lot of love.

descriptions.en: National Women's Day in South Africa marks 9 August 1956, when about 20,000 women marched to the Union Buildings in Pretoria to protest against the extension of apartheid pass laws to women. Led by Lilian Ngoyi, Helen Joseph, Rahima Moosa and Sophia Williams, they left petitions for the prime minister, stood in silence and then sang "Wathint' abafazi, wathint' imbokodo": you strike a woman, you strike a rock. After apartheid ended, the date became a public holiday. Today it honours women's part in the struggle for freedom and keeps attention on gender equality, violence against women and economic opportunity.
